# casa-rs and CASA 6.7.6.14 tasks and tools

Truth class: generated reference
Generated by: `scripts/check-casa-inventory.py --write`
Sources: `resources/casa-compat/casa-6.7.6.14/` (read from CASA by `tools/casa-compat/dump_casa_task_inventory.py`), `crates/casa-provider-contracts/resources/parameter-surfaces.json`, `parameter-catalog.json`, the CASA class signatures in `crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/`, and reviewed `resources/casa-compat/semantics/`

> Do not edit this file by hand. Regenerate it after changing the inventory, a surface, a recorded class signature or a reviewed file.

Each casa-rs task that mimics a CASA task (#931) against that task as CASA 6.7.6.14 defines it: whether it presents CASA's signature, the CASA parameters casa-rs does not take yet, those it takes but accepts only at CASA's default, the parameters casa-rs takes that CASA does not (casa-rs names for CASA concepts, or casa-rs-only controls), whether the shared parameters keep CASA's order, and the defaults that differ. `calibrate`, `msconvert` and `msexplore` are casa-rs tasks with no CASA counterpart.

The CASA parameters casa-rs lacks or accepts only at their defaults are tracked by family: images in #977, MeasurementSet and flagging in #978, calibration in #979 and `tclean` in #980.

For direct `cBool`, `cFloat`, `cInt`, `cPath` and `cStr` schemas with the recorded coercions, a value both implementations reject for type reports CASA's wording, unless a narrower unimplemented-form diagnostic applies. Direct `cBoolVec`, `cFloatVec`, `cIntVec`, `cPathVec` and `cStrVec` schemas are also covered where the recorded vector coercions apply. Float-shaped `cIntVec` inputs keep the native diagnostic because a JSON integer outside the native range may lose its original spelling. For explicit scalar inputs checked by the task, a missing absolute or explicitly relative path gets CASA's wording when the schema has one direct required path. Other required-path cases, unions and variants retain casa-rs's diagnostics (#1099). CASA accepts booleans as integers and coerces them to floats; where casa-rs refuses one, it keeps its own message. Exception classes follow the casa-rs Python contract.

#### applycal interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="applycal-behavior-common-application"></a>
##### Apply chains while preserving unselected data and calibrated weight semantics

**Implemented** — Ordinary and partitioned MeasurementSets, shared selectors and Python input forms, supported G/T/B/BPOLY/K and routine priors, calibration libraries, all six modes, backup, HISTORY and standalone parang.

New calibration families remain on their owning tickets under #979. Detailed performance tuning and final qualification follow functionality on #979.

Evidence: [oracle](#applycal-evidence-oracle), [mms-oracle](#applycal-evidence-mms-oracle), [performance](#applycal-evidence-performance).

<a id="applycal-behavior-leakage-application"></a>
##### Apply linearized and full-matrix leakage to four polarization products

**Implemented** — Linear and circular four-product data with D, Df, Dgen, Dfgen, DLLS and DfLLS tables. Includes variable time and channel solutions, G/D/P order, flags, missing antennas, subselected channels, and unequal scalar and spectral weights.

The permuted-correlation and malformed-table differences are documented below. Cross-hand phase families continue under #1522.

Evidence: [leakage-application](#applycal-evidence-leakage-application).

#### applycal deviations and unfinished work

##### honor-leakage-correlation-metadata: Previously agreed

- Inputs: A consistent linear-feed CORR_TYPE order of XX, YY, XY, YX.
- CASA: Applies the correction to fixed slots and modifies a parallel hand.
- casa-rs: Applies the leakage correction and flags to the products named by the MeasurementSet.
- Rationale: The four-product layout is valid in casacore. Applying a cross-hand formula to a parallel hand changes the observed data incorrectly.
- User impact: The native output equals permuting the canonical-order result.
- Owner decision: Correct CASA data corruption under the standing deviations rule. [Owner decision](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/issues/1054)
- Evidence: [leakage-application](#applycal-evidence-leakage-application).

##### reject-underspecified-leakage-shape: Previously agreed

- Inputs: A D Jones calibration table with one complex receptor per solution.
- CASA: Aborts with ArrayShapeError.
- casa-rs: Raises a catchable invalid calibration shape error.
- Rationale: Two coefficients are required for a four-product leakage correction.
- User impact: The caller can handle the malformed caltable without losing the process.
- Owner decision: Correct CASA crashes and aborts under the standing deviations rule. [Owner decision](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/issues/1054)
- Evidence: [leakage-application](#applycal-evidence-leakage-application).

#### calstat deviations and unfinished work

##### deterministic-nan-statistics: Proposed

- Inputs: A table column with both numeric values and NaN samples.
- CASA: The median, quartile range and bounds can change when the same NaN moves between rows.
- casa-rs: Preserves deterministic bounds over non-NaN samples, counts every sample and reports undefined moments and quantiles.
- Rationale: The moments and quantiles of the unmasked data are undefined when a sample is NaN.
- User impact: The selected row order does not change the native NaN policy.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#calstat-evidence-paired).

#### fluxscale deviations and unfinished work

##### safe-spectral-orders: Previously agreed

- Record: [Fluxscale negative and underdetermined spectral-fit orders](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/53a1ca6722ae5758f9598487be2395d8b6212205/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#fluxscale-negative-and-underdetermined-spectral-fit-orders)
- Inputs: Negative order, too few valid windows for requested degree, or an exactly determined fit.
- CASA: Can segfault, fit the wrong degree, return unstable coefficients/negative covariance, or invent roundoff uncertainty.
- casa-rs: Use advertised negative-order fallback; cap degree at nvalid-1, pad requested vectors and retain zero residual uncertainty at zero residual degrees of freedom.
- Rationale: Implement identifiable fits and CASA's advertised fallback while retaining existing strict linear-fit behavior.
- User impact: Determined fits agree; invalid memory access and unstable underdetermined artifacts are corrected.
- Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
- Evidence: [oracle](#fluxscale-evidence-oracle).

##### initialized-history-and-empty-map: Previously agreed

- Record: [Fluxscale history can contain uninitialized object identifiers](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/53a1ca6722ae5758f9598487be2395d8b6212205/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#fluxscale-history-can-contain-uninitialized-object-identifiers)
- Inputs: Successful MS HISTORY writes or refspwmap=[].
- CASA: Does not initialize OBJECT_ID; indexes an empty map and segfaults.
- casa-rs: Initialize OBJECT_ID=0 and treat the empty map as identity.
- Rationale: Avoid uninitialized scientific provenance and invalid memory access.
- User impact: Stable provenance; empty mapping is safe.
- Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
- Evidence: [oracle](#fluxscale-evidence-oracle).

##### preserve-scientific-files: Previously agreed

- Record: [Fluxscale listfile can overwrite scientific table files](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/53a1ca6722ae5758f9598487be2395d8b6212205/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#fluxscale-listfile-can-overwrite-scientific-table-files)
- Inputs: A listing path inside the input MS, input caltable or output product, or a failed listing stream.
- CASA: Can truncate a scientific table file or report success despite an unchecked stream failure.
- casa-rs: Refuse overlapping paths before mutation and report listing write failures.
- Rationale: Preserve scientific data and fulfill the requested text output.
- User impact: Potentially destructive paths are refused; ordinary listing paths work.
- Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
- Evidence: [oracle](#fluxscale-evidence-oracle).

<a id="gencal-behavior-positions"></a>
##### Antenna offsets and service inputs

Compared with the installed CASA reference.

Evidence: [manual-positions](#gencal-evidence-manual-positions), [vla-archive](#gencal-evidence-vla-archive), [alma-service](#gencal-evidence-alma-service).

<a id="gencal-behavior-switched-power"></a>
##### VLA switched-power gains and visibility weights

**Implemented** — Generate, overwrite and apply CASA G EVLASWPOW tables from SYSPOWER and CALDEVICE for the five switched-power modes. Preserve the separate visibility gains and Tsys weight factors and share application with solver preapply.

Compared with the installed CASA reference.

Evidence: [switched-power](#gencal-evidence-switched-power).

<a id="gencal-behavior-jyperk"></a>
##### ALMA Jy/K factor files and service

**Implemented** — Read receptor-specific CSV factors and generate CASA-readable G Jones tables with cumulative positive gains. Compare queries, calibrated tables and fallback for ASDM, interpolation and model fit. Test the public ASDM service separately.

Dedicated dataset-scale performance validation remains in #979.

Evidence: [jyperk](#gencal-evidence-jyperk).

<a id="gencal-behavior-tecim"></a>
##### Ionosphere correction from a vertical TEC cube

**Implemented** — Interpolate TEC in world coordinates and convert it to line-of-sight electron content. Apply dispersive phase and Faraday rotation across both feed bases without scaling weights.

Dedicated dataset-scale performance validation remains in #979.

Evidence: [tecim](#gencal-evidence-tecim).

<a id="gencal-behavior-eop"></a>
##### Earth-orientation corrections and fringe rate

**Implemented** — Calculate phase, delay and rate from recorded Earth orientation and IERS or USNO updates. Use recorded observation and scan geometry, including attached ephemerides. Apply CASA-readable Fringe Jones tables to data and solver inputs.

Dedicated dataset-scale performance validation remains in #979.

Evidence: [eop](#gencal-evidence-eop).

#### gencal deviations and unfinished work

##### safe-whole-axis-selection: Previously agreed

- Record: [Explicit gencal wildcards can index outside the calibration array](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#explicit-gencal-wildcards-can-index-outside-the-calibration-array)
- Inputs: An explicit whole-axis wildcard, a negated antenna index, or an empty legacy VLA antenna selection.
- CASA: Some of these selections abort the process when they index a nonexistent table element.
- casa-rs: Whole-axis selections broadcast, and invalid negative antenna indices raise a task error.
- Rationale: Prevent native crashes and preserve prior calibration products.
- User impact: Explicit and equivalent all-antenna selections produce the same intended correction.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [specified](#gencal-evidence-specified), [manual-positions](#gencal-evidence-manual-positions).

##### safe-scalar-opacity: Previously agreed

- Record: [Opacity priors can index a nonexistent second receptor](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#opacity-priors-can-index-a-nonexistent-second-receptor)
- Inputs: A scalar opacity table with a second-receptor or two-receptor selection.
- CASA: Indexes a nonexistent second receptor and terminates the task process.
- casa-rs: Raises a task error and preserves the existing product.
- Rationale: The opacity coefficient is scalar and the requested selection cannot be applied.
- User impact: Empty and first-receptor selectors remain usable.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [opacity](#gencal-evidence-opacity).

##### safe-switched-power-input: Previously agreed

- Record: [A one-receptor SYSPOWER shape aborts switched-power calibration](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#a-one-receptor-syspower-shape-aborts-switched-power-calibration)
- Inputs: One receptor per SYSPOWER measurement or a SYSPOWER timestamp between visibility scans.
- CASA: A malformed receptor shape aborts. An empty scan match is dereferenced and returned 0 in the oracle.
- casa-rs: Refuses malformed shapes before publication and assigns unknown scan -1 to timestamps without a matching scan.
- Rationale: Avoid process termination and retain physical measurement timestamps.
- User impact: Usable SYSPOWER samples retain their actual times. Samples with no matching visibility scan carry an unknown scan ID.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [switched-power](#gencal-evidence-switched-power).

##### finite-jyperk-gains: Previously agreed

- Record: [Invalid Jy/K factors can publish unflagged nonfinite gains](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#invalid-jyk-factors-can-publish-unflagged-nonfinite-gains)
- Inputs: Zero or negative factors, or repeated factors exceeding the representable gain range.
- CASA: Can publish unflagged nonfinite or zero complex gains.
- casa-rs: Refuses the correction before publishing either a fresh or updated product.
- Rationale: An unusable gain can corrupt calibrated visibilities.
- User impact: Usable gains retain CASA multiplication and selector semantics.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [jyperk](#gencal-evidence-jyperk).

##### flag-incomplete-tec: Previously agreed

- Record: [A flagged F Jones coefficient can leave unflagged visibilities](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#a-flagged-f-jones-coefficient-can-leave-unflagged-visibilities)
- Inputs: A circular-feed F Jones table with the last antenna flagged at every epoch.
- CASA: Leaves that antenna with a unity gain and unflagged baseline outputs.
- casa-rs: Flags baselines with an unavailable correction when the apply mode writes flags.
- Rationale: Preserve the validity of calibrated visibilities when a term is missing.
- User impact: Valid solutions continue to apply using CASA science and flags.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [tecim](#gencal-evidence-tecim).

##### preserve-empty-eop-destination: Previously agreed

- Record: [An empty EOP result can delete an existing calibration table](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#an-empty-eop-result-can-delete-an-existing-calibration-table)
- Inputs: An existing Fringe Jones table and a missing input file or input without matching Earth orientation updates.
- CASA: Removes the destination during cleanup.
- casa-rs: Keeps the existing table and only publishes a complete replacement.
- Rationale: Preserve prior calibration products on input failures.
- User impact: A missing input still raises FileNotFoundError. No matching Earth orientation leaves a diagnostic and preserves any prior product.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [eop](#gencal-evidence-eop).

##### bracket-all-eop-samples: Previously agreed

- Record: [EOP interpolation can ignore later daily samples](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/93fa3061e84c7359e18c837ec22aff1089989540/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#eop-interpolation-can-ignore-later-daily-samples)
- Inputs: An observing epoch after the fourth day in a daily Earth orientation series.
- CASA: Caps the upper sample index at three and extrapolates from earlier samples.
- casa-rs: Brackets the observing epoch using the available samples.
- Rationale: Prevent a stale polar-motion or UT1 correction despite available matching data.
- User impact: The seven-epoch fixture agrees with an independent ERFA delay calculation.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [eop](#gencal-evidence-eop).

#### getjyperkalma deviations and unfinished work

##### finite-jyperk-gains: Previously agreed

- Record: [Invalid Jy/K factors can publish unflagged nonfinite gains](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/0886835f74c8d8215774fd93b1577fad093d9321/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#invalid-jyk-factors-can-publish-unflagged-nonfinite-gains)
- Inputs: Zero or negative factors, or repeated factors exceeding the representable gain range.
- CASA: Can publish unflagged nonfinite or zero complex gains.
- casa-rs: Refuses the correction before publishing either a fresh or updated product.
- Rationale: An unusable gain can corrupt calibrated visibilities.
- User impact: Usable gains retain CASA multiplication and selector semantics.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [jyperk](#getjyperkalma-evidence-jyperk).

#### initweights interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="initweights-behavior-ordinary"></a>
##### Ordinary weights and channel spectra

**Implemented** — Six numerical and spectrum-management modes across absent, complete and partly defined spectra. Includes Multi-MS, flagged visibilities and a 122,880-row casacore readback across the native write-batch boundary. Includes refusal of a zero-row MS.

The compared MS products matched CASA.

Evidence: [ordinary](#initweights-evidence-ordinary).

<a id="initweights-behavior-tsys"></a>
##### Tsys weight initialization

**Implemented** — Both temperature modes with gain-field selection, channel and time interpolation, explicit and relative spectral-window mappings, flagged and invalid temperatures, FLOAT_DATA, and scalar and spectrum outputs. Includes relative paths, single-correlation Stokes I and missing calibration windows.

The compared MS products matched CASA. Invalid selections are handled as described below.

Evidence: [tsys](#initweights-evidence-tsys).

#### initweights deviations and unfinished work

##### validate-before-spectrum-creation: Proposed

- Inputs: Tsys with dowtsp enabled and an invalid gain-field or interpolation setting.
- CASA: Throws RuntimeError and can leave newly added spectrum columns undefined.
- casa-rs: Throws RuntimeError before creating either spectrum column.
- Rationale: Validate the table, field selection and interpolation before changing the MS.
- User impact: A rejected call leaves the original spectrum schema available for retry.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [tsys](#initweights-evidence-tsys).

#### listcal interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="listcal-behavior-solution-listing"></a>
##### Selected calibration solution listings

**Implemented** — Complex gain and bandpass values, real delay and fringe units, flags, field and antenna selectors, channel ranges and strides, multiple spectral windows, repeated physical integrations, terminal paging and atomic text output. Includes relative symlink paths, non-finite formatting, invalid arguments, baseline and unknown types, and a later spectral-window error after the first prompt.

The incomplete-antenna error behavior is recorded below.

Evidence: [paired](#listcal-evidence-paired).

#### listcal deviations and unfinished work

##### reject-incomplete-antenna-integration: Proposed

- Inputs: A standard G Jones calibration solution table with the final antenna row removed.
- CASA: Terminates after opening the output while reshaping the window into antenna blocks.
- casa-rs: Raises a recoverable layout error before publishing the output.
- Rationale: An incomplete block cannot be associated with the requested antenna solutions.
- User impact: The caller can handle the error and the listing path remains available for a corrected retry.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#listcal-evidence-paired).

#### plotbandpass interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-selection"></a>
##### Antenna, field, window, scan and solution time

**Implemented** — Select current calibration rows by antenna and field names or IDs, spectral-window and baseband numbers, scan numbers and solution times. Apply the pinned CASA type and domain validation and retain the recorded return type for empty selections.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-spectra"></a>
##### Bandpass and Tsys plots

**Implemented** — Plot current complex B and real Tsys solutions and legacy BPOLY curves. Read the associated MS metadata, honor flags and receptor choices, and overlay one B or up to two BPOLY companions through the shared plot document.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-axes"></a>
##### Plot axes and spectral windows

**Implemented** — Use channel or frequency coordinates with amplitude, phase, dB, delay or temperature units. Apply explicit limits, channel windows and the CASA narrower-solution rule for comparison zoom. Draw FDM windows and label mapped baseband numbers.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-presentation"></a>
##### Page layout, display, PNG and PDF products

**Implemented** — Draw and page through the selected panels, including backward movement, early exit and EOF. Apply marker and line settings, density and calibrated filenames. Assemble PDFs with the selected local converter and document tools.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-atmosphere"></a>
##### Atmospheric transmission, sky and image-sideband curves

**Implemented** — Evaluate the native ATM profile using the calibration frequency grid, station conditions, pointing and field metadata, and requested or measured PWV. Recover the image oscillator from receiver metadata and parent window names when supplied.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

<a id="plotbandpass-behavior-derivative"></a>
##### Channel derivatives and platforming

**Implemented** — Plot channel differences, report MAD and standard deviation, and include medians and platforming events in the typed result. Use the configured edge exclusion and thresholds. Reproduce the installed CASA error for derivative resampling greater than one.



Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

#### plotbandpass deviations and unfinished work

##### integer-platforming-channel-bounds: Proposed

- Inputs: Channel derivatives with enough interior points to enter the platforming check.
- CASA: Passes floating-point channel offsets to Python range and raises TypeError.
- casa-rs: Uses integer channel indices and tests the interior derivative against the requested MAD or percentage threshold.
- Rationale: Keep the documented platforming check functional for wide calibration spectral windows.
- User impact: An interior amplitude step is reported at a threshold it exceeds and omitted at a larger threshold.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

##### default-atmosphere-without-weather: Proposed

- Inputs: An atmospheric overlay on a bandpass whose associated MS has no WEATHER table.
- CASA: Raises NameError while referencing needToClose_mymsmd.
- casa-rs: Evaluates the ATM profile using the station defaults available in the absence of measured weather.
- Rationale: Allow a transmission or sky-temperature overlay for supported data with missing weather measurements.
- User impact: The plot includes a finite atmospheric curve and the original calibration spectra.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#plotbandpass-evidence-paired).

#### plotbandpass evidence

Evidence is scoped to its named revision, inputs and comparator. Historical reported results need applicability review; planned or unexecuted tests are not passes.

##### paired

**Same-input public Python tasks and Matplotlib artist arrays — passed.** 41 plot cases, seven terminal cases, 24 argument and domain cases, 76 rendered panels, paired two-page PDFs and two analytic platforming thresholds passed. Default atmospheric conditions were verified when WEATHER was absent. CASA 6.7.6.14 plots and return values, including selected arrays, axes, titles, companion time grids, physical receptor labels, masking, overlay colors and legends, paging, PNG filenames, PDFs, measured water, wide atmospheric grids and split receivers.

#### plotms interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="plotms-behavior-table"></a>
##### Read MeasurementSets and calibration tables

**Partial** — Open casacore MeasurementSets and current, BPOLY and GSPLINE calibration tables through vis or caltable, preserving the public None return and input-path checks.

Remaining MeasurementSet plotting paths are open under #1032 and #215.

Evidence: [paired](#plotms-evidence-paired), [legacy-calibration](#plotms-evidence-legacy-calibration).

<a id="plotms-behavior-selection"></a>
##### Select solution samples

**Partial** — Select solution rows and channels by field, window, time, antenna, scan, observation, polarization, antenna-position component and TaQL. Refuse unsupported modern calibration selectors. Resolve GSPLINE selection directly against source table rows and CAL_DESC. Route ordinary MeasurementSet visibility plots through native row, baseline, channel, correlation and flag selection.

Remaining MeasurementSet selection paths are open under #1032 and #215.

Evidence: [paired](#plotms-evidence-paired), [selectors](#plotms-evidence-selectors), [ms-ordinary-visibility](#plotms-evidence-ms-ordinary-visibility), [legacy-calibration](#plotms-evidence-legacy-calibration).

<a id="plotms-behavior-coordinates"></a>
##### Project axes and flags

**Partial** — Read complex and real parameter cells and select calibration axes. Keep flagged sample visibility consistent in text and image products. Validate active axis and range controls before writing. Use the reference axes for Tsys and antenna-position products. Evaluate stored BPOLY and GSPLINE coefficients and expose their solution flags and metadata. Plot independent stored MeasurementSet DATA, CORRECTED_DATA and MODEL_DATA axes and unaveraged vector and scalar residuals or model ratios with the shared sample mask. Use DATA for corrected axes, residuals and ratios when the stored corrected column is absent on a complex MeasurementSet. Use FLOAT_DATA for observed visibilities on unaveraged mixed inputs and signed amplitude or real axes on float-only inputs. Keep the requested order and column identity for two independent unaveraged ordinates. Use the default visibility model for complex data without a stored model or an applicable virtual recipe.

Pointing-coordinate axes, more than two ordinates, averaged independent ordinate columns and additional MS column forms are open.

Evidence: [paired](#plotms-evidence-paired), [selectors](#plotms-evidence-selectors), [ms-columns](#plotms-evidence-ms-columns), [ms-residual-columns](#plotms-evidence-ms-residual-columns), [ms-scalar-residual-columns](#plotms-evidence-ms-scalar-residual-columns), [ms-model-ratios](#plotms-evidence-ms-model-ratios), [ms-ordinate-columns](#plotms-evidence-ms-ordinate-columns), [ms-float-data](#plotms-evidence-ms-float-data), [ms-corrected-fallback](#plotms-evidence-ms-corrected-fallback), [callibrary](#plotms-evidence-callibrary), [legacy-calibration](#plotms-evidence-legacy-calibration), [ms-default-model](#plotms-evidence-ms-default-model).

<a id="plotms-behavior-averaging"></a>
##### Average solution points

Renderer-specific marker fill patterns and interactive editing remain open.

Export calibrated MeasurementSet text and paginated figures, including atmospheric curves.

#### plotms deviations and unfinished work

##### disable-selection: Proposed

- Record: [PlotMS disabling selection calls the selection setter with a missing argument](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/b60d8a6a140bd6f0a29177584db5ff91244f5d12/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#plotms-disabling-selection-calls-the-selection-setter-with-a-missing-argument)
- Inputs: A PlotMS request with selectdata=False and supplied selection text.
- CASA: Raises Exception with message updateImmediately must be a boolean.
- casa-rs: Displays and exports all available solution points without applying the selector text.
- Rationale: Make the documented selection switch work when it is false.
- User impact: The native request produces all 160 available points in the paired fixture. The same fallback preserves all 1,920 points in the unfiltered callibrary case.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#plotms-evidence-paired), [callibrary](#plotms-evidence-callibrary).

##### calibration-selection-diagnostics: Proposed

- Inputs: Modern calibration input with an unsupported selector, invalid antenna-position selector or empty TaQL selection.
- CASA: Refuses the plot with an RPC failure whose details say plot parameters failed.
- casa-rs: Refuses the plot with a task parameter error describing the selector or empty row set.
- Rationale: Give the caller the cause using the native task error contract.
- User impact: Both workflows preserve an absent export on selection failure.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [selectors](#plotms-evidence-selectors).

##### gspline-negative-antenna: Proposed

- Record: [PlotMS shows the excluded antenna on a GSPLINE plot](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/b60d8a6a140bd6f0a29177584db5ff91244f5d12/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#plotms-shows-the-excluded-antenna-on-a-gspline-plot)
- Inputs: A five-antenna GSPLINE table plotted with antenna="!A2".
- CASA: Displays only antenna A2, despite negation.
- casa-rs: Displays A0, A1, A3 and A4.
- Rationale: Honor the documented antenna exclusion instead of passing the excluded ID to the plot cache.
- User impact: The displayed antenna membership follows the source-row filter.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [legacy-calibration](#plotms-evidence-legacy-calibration).

#### sdatmcor interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-inputs"></a>
##### Open and select a total-power MeasurementSet

**Implemented** — Resolve selected autocorrelation rows and polarization and read the requested data plane. Apply correction to eligible on-source integrations.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-windows"></a>
##### Resolve independent processing and output windows

**Implemented** — Correct the intersection of processing and output windows. Preserve other output windows and map each output spectrum to its original channels.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-gain"></a>
##### Apply calibration-derived gain

**Implemented** — Accept the scalar, per-window mapping, or a calibration table. Apply the window gain to the additive atmospheric correction.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-atmosphere"></a>
##### Use measured weather, pointing, and the atmospheric profile

**Implemented** — Use recorded ambient conditions by default and allow explicit site and atmospheric overrides. Interpolate pointing, link target and reference elevations, and use the native atmospheric model and measured band response.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-layers"></a>
##### Configure detailed ATM layers

**Implemented** — Accept profile and layer quantities, default values and unit strings. The pinned layer model accepts a pressure factor but computes with a fixed factor of 1.075.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

<a id="sdatmcor-behavior-output"></a>
##### Publish an interoperable corrected MeasurementSet

**Implemented** — Write the selected MeasurementSet, including unchanged imaginary components, flags and weights. Stage the replacement until processing succeeds.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

#### sdatmcor deviations and unfinished work

##### empty-processing-intersection: Previously agreed

- Record: [An empty atmospheric correction window selection raises a record-type error](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c79ffdb24ad34d102117217f110217ae0f6581c3/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#an-empty-atmospheric-correction-window-selection-raises-a-record-type-error)
- Inputs: Use spw='19', outputspw='23' on X320b_sel2.ms.
- CASA: The empty NumPy record list is inferred as floating point and rejected.
- casa-rs: Use a typed empty window list and write the selected spectra unchanged.
- Rationale: There are zero eligible windows for correction.
- User impact: Disjoint processing and output selections produce the selected data.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

##### cropped-channel-coordinates: Previously agreed

- Record: [Atmospheric correction can index a cropped window from channel zero](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c79ffdb24ad34d102117217f110217ae0f6581c3/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#atmospheric-correction-can-index-a-cropped-window-from-channel-zero)
- Inputs: Use outputspw='19:370~407^2' on X320b_sel2.ms.
- CASA: Subtracts corrections computed for channels 0 through 18 from the selected output channels.
- casa-rs: Subtract the correction at each original selected channel.
- Rationale: Original frequency determines the atmospheric signature; the corrected output matches the same channels of a full-window correction.
- User impact: Cropped spectra agree with the requested ordered projection of the full corrected product.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

##### nonfinite-correction: Previously agreed

- Record: [Atmospheric correction can publish unflagged nonfinite spectra](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c79ffdb24ad34d102117217f110217ae0f6581c3/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#atmospheric-correction-can-publish-unflagged-nonfinite-spectra)
- Inputs: Use a calibration table with zero amplitude or a scalar factor of 1e40 for SPW 19.
- CASA: The corrected MeasurementSet contains unflagged nonfinite samples.
- casa-rs: Refuse nonfinite gains and corrections outside the Float32 range before publication.
- Rationale: A gain factor cannot make a finite input spectrum invalid without an error.
- User impact: A failed overwrite preserves an existing finite product.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdatmcor-evidence-paired).

Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing forms or combinations; Default only is derived from the runtime refusal contract; Not implemented has no implementation; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below. No signature or return-structure result establishes scientific equivalence.

Audit baseline: `c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385`. Status counts: Default only: 0, Implemented: 38, Not implemented: 0, Partial: 0, Unassessed: 0.

Mappings, defaults, catalog domains, constraints and conditional default-only refusals are generated from the existing task contract. The catalog may admit values that the native reader then refuses: the reviewed scope and linked combinations describe those restrictions.

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

Release-scale performance follows functionality under #979.

Release-scale performance follows functionality under #979.

Evidence: [sinusoidal-wave-selection](#sdbaseline-evidence-sinusoidal-wave-selection), [sinusoidal-debug-performance](#sdbaseline-evidence-sinusoidal-debug-performance).

#### sdbaseline deviations and unfinished work

##### singleton-mask-pairs: Proposed

- Record: [Single-dish baseline tables can contain malformed singleton mask ranges](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-baseline-tables-can-contain-malformed-singleton-mask-ranges)
- Inputs: Select a spectrum whose fitted mask starts with a singleton channel and another disjoint range.
- CASA: The saved mask has an odd endpoint count and CASA refuses to apply it.
- casa-rs: The singleton channel has equal start and end endpoints and the native table applies in CASA.
- Rationale: Every fitted range needs both endpoints to preserve its channels on interchange.
- User impact: Coefficients can be reused after fitting non-contiguous masks.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdbaseline-evidence-paired).

##### remove-spectral-noise: Proposed

- Record: [Single-dish baseline weight updates can fail when removing two columns](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-baseline-weight-updates-can-fail-when-removing-two-columns)
- Inputs: Set updateweight on an input containing both spectral noise columns.
- CASA: The public task raises after producing the data and scalar weights.
- casa-rs: The public task writes the recalculated weights with the two stale columns omitted.
- Rationale: The table API must receive individual column names when dropping both columns.
- User impact: A successful task leaves a usable product and only its current noise estimates.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdbaseline-evidence-paired).

##### per-spectrum-clipped-count: Proposed

- Record: [Single-dish baseline reports accumulate clipped-channel counts](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-baseline-reports-accumulate-clipped-channel-counts)
- Inputs: Reject one spectral channel in each of multiple consecutive integrations.
- CASA: Reports a running clipped-channel count within a visibility buffer.
- casa-rs: Reports the number clipped in that spectrum.
- Rationale: Each row in the diagnostic describes an individual fit.
- User impact: The number describes the channels rejected in the specified spectrum.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdbaseline-evidence-paired).

##### negative-iterations: Proposed

- Record: [Single-dish baseline fitting accepts negative iteration counts in CASA](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-baseline-fitting-accepts-negative-iteration-counts-in-casa)
- Inputs: Set clipniter below zero or num_fitting_max to zero.
- CASA: Converts the result to an unsigned fit count. Zero can return a model without a fit.
- casa-rs: Reports a fitting-iteration validation error.
- Rationale: Fitting a baseline requires at least the initial fit.
- User impact: The wrapper cannot publish unused or uninitialized coefficients as a fitted model.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [iteration-source](#sdbaseline-evidence-iteration-source).

##### dense-spline-accuracy: Proposed

- Record: [Dense single-dish cubic splines can lose numerical accuracy in CASA](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#dense-single-dish-cubic-splines-can-lose-numerical-accuracy-in-casa)
- Inputs: Fit 47 or 93 cubic pieces to a 96-channel seeded Gaussian spectrum.
- CASA: Residuals differ from the independent B-spline least-squares solution.
- casa-rs: An SVD of the design matrix reproduces that solution within 2.2e-8 RMS.
- Rationale: The normal system squares the condition number of a dense spline design.
- User impact: Highly segmented fits retain numerical accuracy.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [automatic-and-spline](#sdbaseline-evidence-automatic-and-spline).

##### line-finder-index-limits: Proposed

- Record: [Single-dish automatic line masks can access invalid channels in CASA](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/c05d0f79dff04cb7949ee8c7d85064017d8cc385/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-automatic-line-masks-can-access-invalid-channels-in-casa)
- Inputs: Select a narrow fitted range or detect a line touching channel zero.
- CASA: Can index before the median array or decrement an unsigned zero channel index.
- casa-rs: Stop an averaging level with fewer than two eligible bins and bound wing extension.
- Rationale: Those cases have no contributing bins or channels beyond the available data.
- User impact: A narrow range can be fitted even if a coarser bin has no eligible channels.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [automatic-and-spline](#sdbaseline-evidence-automatic-and-spline).

#### sdbaseline evidence

Evidence is scoped to its named revision, inputs and comparator. Historical reported results need applicability review; planned or unexecuted tests are not passes.

<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-paired"></a>
##### paired

**Public Python task and tool comparison plus casacore table interchange — passed.** Paired products and independent coefficient, clipping and weight laws passed. Explicit list masks, two polynomial families, both readers, list and task products, flags, metadata, selection, clipping and scalar weights. The reviewed cases cover the retained clipping endpoint, insufficient refit, input overlap, two independent SPW selectors, padding, schema and time lookup.

- [tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_oracle.py](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5995e36027dc7383185a234aca60c8596fd7014e/tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_oracle.py)
- Revision: `5995e36027dc7383185a234aca60c8596fd7014e`; CASA: `6.7.6.14`.
- Command: `CASARS_CALIBRATE_BIN=<calibrate> casa-python tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_oracle.py <new-dir>`.
- Receipt: `https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/pull/1977`.

<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-progress-controls"></a>
##### progress-controls

**Pinned upstream task source inspection — inspected.** The accepted switches do not affect output products. The private CASA task never reads showprogress or minnrow.


<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-performance-smoke"></a>
##### performance-smoke

**Matched public task timing, compact map — measured.** 0.212 s native debug and 0.242 s CASA wall time on the same 240-row workflow. Release and dataset-scale profiling follow functionality parity under #979. 240 selected rows with text, CSV, baseline-table and MeasurementSet products.

- Revision: `5995e36027dc7383185a234aca60c8596fd7014e`; CASA: `6.7.6.14`.
- Command: `CASARS_CALIBRATE_BIN=<calibrate> casa-python tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_oracle.py <new-dir>`.
- Receipt: `https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/pull/1977`.

<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-pending"></a>
##### pending

**Remaining baseline families and masks — planned.** Tracked by #1532. Cubic-spline, sinusoid, variable and automatic masking.


<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-iteration-source"></a>
##### iteration-source

**Pinned upstream inspection and negative-count probe — inspected.** A task call with clipniter=-1 emits no fitted baseline. Casa-rs rejects negative counts. CASA 6.7.6.14 sdbaseline passes clipniter plus one to an unsigned solver count.


<a id="sdbaseline-evidence-automatic-and-spline"></a>
##### automatic-and-spline

**Public task/tool physics, diagnostics and table interchange — passed.** The paired outputs, expected masks, knot boundaries, model coefficients and residual laws agree. Six line masks, a narrow channel stripe, invalid controls, one to three spline pieces, clipping, reports and both table readers. Includes infinite thresholds, unused controls on fully flagged spectra, skipped-receptor metadata and an independent dense-spline comparison.

- [tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_mask_spline_oracle.py](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/9988be830413ce58f7a05b46a413e8de21a0dc46/tools/casa-compat/sdbaseline_mask_spline_oracle.py)

- Receipt: `https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/pull/1978`.

#### sdcal deviations and unfinished work

##### protect-zero-sky-signal: Proposed

- Inputs: A sky calibration table with a clear flag and a zero OFF reference spectrum.
- CASA: Divides by the zero spectrum and leaves the channel unflagged.
- casa-rs: Retains the value entering the sky correction and flags the invalid sample in flag-writing modes.
- Rationale: The OFF spectrum is the denominator of the correction and cannot define a finite calibrated value at zero.
- User impact: Adjacent channels with valid references still calibrate and downstream consumers can mask the invalid correction.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [application](#sdcal-evidence-application).

##### include-raster-final-strip: Proposed

- Inputs: A gapped raster map with multiple strips and valid reference integrations at both ends of each strip.
- CASA: Depending on uninitialized gap-array contents, can omit the two solutions from the last strip.
- casa-rs: Always close the final range at the integration count and select both ends of the last strip.
- Rationale: The last observed strip has the same edge eligibility as preceding strips. Including both boundaries produces stable calibration across repeat runs.
- User impact: All 44 reference spectra from the 22-strip fixture are present.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [edges](#sdcal-evidence-edges).

#### sdfit deviations and unfinished work

##### chronological-time-bins: Previously agreed

- Record: [Single-dish line fitting can exceed its time bin on descending rows](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/f8253b17601ac8d8bf538c516ea05b19a6129891/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-line-fitting-can-exceed-its-time-bin-on-descending-rows)
- Inputs: A one-second fit bin on four integrations provided in descending physical order.
- CASA: The iterator fits one combined spectrum per hand.
- casa-rs: Chronological ordering yields four fitted spectra per hand in either physical row order.
- Rationale: The bin duration applies to integration times. Fit products agree with CASA on the chronological input.
- User impact: A reordered MeasurementSet gives the same fitted time bins.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdfit-evidence-paired).

##### single-hand-average: Previously agreed

- Record: [Single-dish polarization averaging can abort for one selected hand](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/f8253b17601ac8d8bf538c516ea05b19a6129891/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-polarization-averaging-can-abort-for-one-selected-hand)
- Inputs: Select YY on an XX/YY setup and request geometric averaging.
- CASA: The iterator can abort while indexing the original pair.
- casa-rs: With no selected pair, fit the selected hand unchanged.
- Rationale: The selected correlation is the only available eligible spectrum.
- User impact: The call returns the equivalent fit of the selected hand.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdfit-evidence-paired).

##### negative-fit-count: Previously agreed

- Record: [Single-dish line fitting aborts for negative component counts](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/f8253b17601ac8d8bf538c516ea05b19a6129891/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#single-dish-line-fitting-aborts-for-negative-component-counts)
- Inputs: Use nfit=[-1] in list mode.
- CASA: An unsigned component allocation can abort the process.
- casa-rs: Raise a runtime error before allocating a fit.
- Rationale: A component count cannot be negative.
- User impact: The caller can correct the list without losing the session.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdfit-evidence-paired).

##### fit-report-overwrite: Previously agreed

- Record: [A failed line fit can delete the previous report](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/f8253b17601ac8d8bf538c516ea05b19a6129891/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#a-failed-line-fit-can-delete-the-previous-report)
- Inputs: Enable overwrite for an existing fit report and supply a mismatched component count.
- CASA: The earlier report is removed before the error.
- casa-rs: Keep the report until the replacement has been fitted and written.
- Rationale: An incomplete fit cannot replace an existing product.
- User impact: The caller keeps the earlier report after a failed fit.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdfit-evidence-paired).

#### sdgaincal deviations and unfinished work

##### scalar-channel-requirement: Proposed

- Inputs: Select two channels of a three-channel total-power spectral window for a double-circle gain solve.
- CASA: Aborts while copying a two-channel spectrum into a scalar solve cell.
- casa-rs: Returns a catchable error and preserves existing files before publication.
- Rationale: Selecting one channel produces the defined scalar gain shape.
- User impact: A caller can select one channel and rerun without restarting Python.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdgaincal-evidence-paired).

##### no-central-integrations: Proposed

- Inputs: Move the field reference outside the observed map so the pointing filter finds no central integration.
- CASA: Segfaults while constructing time ranges from the empty selection.
- casa-rs: Returns a catchable solve error and preserves existing files.
- Rationale: No central integration is available to normalize gain.
- User impact: A caller can adjust the radius or field and rerun safely.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#sdgaincal-evidence-paired).

#### simobserve interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="simobserve-behavior-sky-model"></a>
##### Sky model and component list

**Partial** — skymodel through modifymodel and flatimage with inbright, indirection, incell, incenter and inwidth; complist with compwidth and comp_nchan, alone or with a sky model.

Scoped CASA task evidence covers scalar indirection and incell overrides separately and together, four-channel component-only models, combined image/component inputs with brightness/cell/direction/frequency overrides, and a polarized four-Stokes, four-channel image with components. The receipts cover these representative workflows, not an exhaustive Cartesian product of inputs.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [model-overrides-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-model-overrides-20261111), [main-integration-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-main-integration-20261111), [interferometric-projects-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-interferometric-projects-20261114).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-antennas"></a>
##### Antenna lists

**Implemented** — antennalist and sdantlist as files, ALMA resolution strings ('alma;0.5arcsec'), the search through the project directory and CASA's alma/simmos, and sdant.

Named configurations require external public alma/simmos files in a valid CASA_RS_MEASURESPATH or ~/.casa/data runtime. README describes obtaining them from NRAO's runtime-data archive; the compact measures snapshot does not bundle them. Project-local and explicit configuration files remain supported.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [uvw-long-baselines-20261112](#simobserve-evidence-uvw-long-baselines-20261112), [array-configuration-controls](#simobserve-evidence-array-configuration-controls).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-pointings"></a>
##### Pointings

**Partial** — setpointings with direction, mapsize, maptype and pointingspacing, or a ptgfile; written to <stem>.ptg.txt and checked against the model.

CASA task evidence includes square interferometric pointings, a three-entry user pointing file with 10/20/30-second dwell times over two full passes, and a 16 by 12 arcsecond hexagonal map with explicit 4 arcsecond spacing. Other file formats and pointing/model/mode combinations remain outside these receipts.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [scheduling-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-scheduling-20261111), [pointings-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-pointings-20261111), [main-integration-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-main-integration-20261111).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-schedule"></a>
##### Calibrator and observing schedule

**Partial** — caldirection and calflux, integration, totaltime, refdate and hourangle.

Paired task evidence now covers numeric and quantity non-transit hour angles, reference dates in 2015/2016/2017/2025 and discarded time suffixes. The historical calibrator cases still use CASA sm re-prediction because the CASA task leaves calibrator scans unpredicted (approved decision); these four new cases have no calibrator.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [scheduling-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-scheduling-20261111), [main-integration-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-main-integration-20261111), [uvw-long-baselines-20261112](#simobserve-evidence-uvw-long-baselines-20261112).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-observation"></a>
##### Observation and prediction

**Partial** — obsmode 'int', 'sd' and '' (corrupting an existing MeasurementSet), outframe, and the prediction of the model and calibrator.

Image-model interferometry has scoped CASA comparisons for LSRK, TOPO, BARY, LSRD, GEO, GALACTO, LGROUP and CMB. REST image prediction succeeds; Undefined image/component predictions and REST component or joint predictions resolve to documented failures before native MS publication. Stateful controls also cover continuation of REST image and BARY MeasurementSets, an ignored Undefined output-frame request, single-dish continuation, manual/atmospheric noise and ignored leakage with prediction disabled; original MS spectral frames are preserved. These are scoped workflows rather than an exhaustive Cartesian product of inputs.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [frequency-frames-20261106](#simobserve-evidence-frequency-frames-20261106), [additional-frames-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-additional-frames-20261111), [main-integration-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-main-integration-20261111), [uvw-long-baselines-20261112](#simobserve-evidence-uvw-long-baselines-20261112), [interferometric-projects-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-interferometric-projects-20261114), [project-lifecycle-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-project-lifecycle-20261114).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-noise"></a>
##### Thermal noise and leakage

**Partial** — thermalnoise 'tsys-atm', 'tsys-manual' and '' with user_pwv, t_ground, t_sky, tau0, seed, leakage and correlator.

Noise is compared statistically (variances and KS tests), since draws differ; each environment parameter is exercised once; seed is casa-rs's own stream. CASA's own suite holds its noise tests to CASA's seed-11111 draws within 5%, which casa-rs's random stream cannot reproduce; over 20 seeds the two implementations' noise levels agree to 0.5%.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [casa-suite-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-casa-suite-20261103), [noise-seeds-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-noise-seeds-20261103).

<a id="simobserve-behavior-outputs"></a>
##### Files, overwrite and graphics

**Implemented** — CASA's file names under the project, overwrite, verbose and graphics.

Complete image/component/dense-pointing/single-dish figures, file/screen/both/none and public simulation helpers have scoped CASA comparisons. PNG rendering requires the Python host and plot extra; direct headless use without its payload warns. These are representative workflows, not an exhaustive Cartesian product of inputs.

Evidence: [task-tests](#simobserve-evidence-task-tests), [parity-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-parity-20261103), [casa-suite-20261103](#simobserve-evidence-casa-suite-20261103), [quick-psf-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-quick-psf-20261111), [quick-psf-relative-project-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-quick-psf-relative-project-20261111), [project-lifecycle-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-project-lifecycle-20261114), [graphics-20261111](#simobserve-evidence-graphics-20261111), [simulation-figures-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-simulation-figures-20261114).

#### simobserve deviations and unfinished work

##### compwidth-unset-spectral-increment: Previously agreed

- Record: [An unset `compwidth` gives the component-only model a meaningless spectral increment](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#an-unset-compwidth-gives-the-component-only-model-a-meaningless-spectral-increment)
- Inputs: simobserve with a component list, no sky image and compwidth=''.
- CASA: It observes 2 GHz when compwidth is not a quantity, but sets the .compskymodel spectral increment from compwidth anyway, yielding a meaningless value (the RA in radians read as hertz, 4.976 Hz for RA 19h, in CASA 6.7.6).
- casa-rs: Uses the 2 GHz simobserve observes with.
- Rationale: The increment is the model's only spectral information beyond its reference frequency.
- User impact: The component-only model carries a consistent spectral increment.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### calibrator-last-pass-scans-lists: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve's calibrator: the last pass, its scans and two component lists](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserves-calibrator-the-last-pass-its-scans-and-two-component-lists)
- Inputs: simobserve with a phase calibrator (caldirection and calflux), also with a complist or totaltime ending inside a pass.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6 never observes the pointings of an incomplete last pass (a 300 s total on 105 pointings has only the calibrator's scan), selects fields range(0,nfld) so the calibrator's scans keep zeros plus noise, and joins component lists into one nonexistent table so predict returns False.
- casa-rs: Observes the pointings the time allows, predicts every scan including the calibrator's, and predicts both lists as one list of their components.
- Rationale: The task means to observe and predict all of these.
- User impact: CASA data can lack pointings, have unpredicted calibrator scans, or be all zero; casa-rs data are complete (parity cases agree at 5e-9 NRMS).
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### noisier-t-cal-left: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve leaves `<stem>.noisier.T.cal`](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserve-leaves-stemnoisiertcal)
- Inputs: simobserve with tsys-atm noise set after leakage (the noisier measurement set).
- CASA: The setnoise table is written beside the noisy MeasurementSet, and the clean-up deletes <stem>.noisy.T.cal and <stem>.noisy.sd.T.cal but not <stem>.noisier.T.cal.
- casa-rs: Writes no Tsys table for any of the three.
- Rationale: The table is a by-product the task means to remove.
- User impact: CASA leaves a stray table in the project that casa-rs never creates.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### observing-loop-never-ends: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve's observing loop never ends for pointings of no length](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserves-observing-loop-never-ends-for-pointings-of-no-length)
- Inputs: simobserve with integration='0s' or a pointing file of zero times.
- CASA: The while (sttime-scanstart) < totalsec loop advances by each pointing's scan length; when a pass's lengths sum to zero the time never advances and CASA loops forever, collecting pointings.
- casa-rs: Refuses such a schedule with a message.
- Rationale: A schedule with no length cannot be observed.
- User impact: The task stops with an error instead of hanging.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### skymodel-deleted-when-output: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve deletes a sky model that is the model it writes](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserve-deletes-a-sky-model-that-is-the-model-it-writes)
- Inputs: simobserve with skymodel given as the full path <project>/<stem>.skymodel (e.g. a rerun on an earlier run's model) and overwrite=True.
- CASA: The output is the input: CASA deletes the model and then fails to read it.
- casa-rs: Refuses the input, and the model is left in place.
- Rationale: The user's input must not be destroyed.
- User impact: The model survives and the user gets a clear refusal.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### project-path-nests-in-itself: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve nests a project path inside itself](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserve-nests-a-project-path-inside-itself)
- Inputs: simobserve with project given as a path, e.g. 'a/b'.
- CASA: The task names files fileroot + '/' + project + '.' + cfg, so 'a/b' gives a/b/a/b.<cfg> in a directory that does not exist; only a plain name in the working directory works.
- casa-rs: Names files by the directory's last component, a/b/b.<cfg>.
- Rationale: For a plain name the two are the same.
- User impact: Project paths work in casa-rs and fail in CASA.
- Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### symlink-in-project-write-through: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve writes through a symbolic link in the project](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserve-writes-through-a-symbolic-link-in-the-project)
- Inputs: simobserve overwrite=True in a project containing a symbolic link such as <stem>.ptg.txt.
- CASA: CASA copies ptgfile through the link, replacing the file the link points to outside the project, and creates outside files for dangling links; links to tables stop the task via rmtree; existence checks follow links.
- casa-rs: Replaces a link in the project with the new file or table, leaves the target alone, and counts a link as existing under overwrite=False.
- Rationale: Owner's decision of 2026-10-26: only the project's own files are replaced.
- User impact: Files outside the project are no longer overwritten or created through links.
- Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-26: the project's own files are the only ones overwrite replaces (recorded with the provider contracts' overwrite exception).
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### direction-list-of-one-mean: Previously agreed

- Record: [simobserve rounds a `direction` list of one to its mean](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/49c810c57210127fc4bc4f66289cadec90f49947/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#simobserve-rounds-a-direction-list-of-one-to-its-mean)
- Inputs: simobserve with direction=['J2000 18h00m00.123456789s ...'] (a list of one) versus the same direction as a string.
- CASA: CASA passes the list to calc_pointings2, and direction_splitter centres it at its mean written at precision 5, so the map is laid out about 1e-5 s of RA (0.15 mas) from the string case.
- casa-rs: casa-rs's simutil follows CASA, but simobserve treats a list of one like a string and lays the map out at the exact direction.
- Rationale: The task contract resolves a string to a list of one, and the rounding carries no information.
- User impact: A map is placed at the exact direction, differing from CASA by about 0.15 mas for a list of one.
- Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#simobserve-evidence-bugs-record).

##### report-failed-frequency-predictions: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Interferometric simobserve with Undefined output frames, or REST frames and component inputs/calibrators.
- CASA: The simulator rejects frequency conversion with predict=False; simobserve ignores it, succeeds and publishes zero unpredicted DATA.
- casa-rs: Report the simulator failure cause before close publishes an unpredicted MS; preserve prepared model/pointing products and support valid REST image prediction.
- Rationale: A rejected prediction cannot produce a valid simulated science dataset. Do not hide the failure behind a successful zero-MS task result.
- User impact: Scripts now receive the calculation error instead of silently continuing with invalid DATA. Valid other frame/model combinations are unchanged.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: where CASA loses/corrupts data or contradicts its evident intent, casa-rs corrects it. This applies that existing policy to ignored predict=False outcomes.
- Evidence: [interferometric-projects-20261114](#simobserve-evidence-interferometric-projects-20261114).

<a id="simobserve-evidence-casa-suite-20261103"></a>
##### casa-suite-20261103

**CASA's test_task_simobserve with casa-rs in place of CASA's task — measured.** Of the 54 cases CASA 6.7.6.14 passes on this host, casa-rs passes 45. Of the other 9, 3 refuse as CASA does in casa-rs's own words: an empty project, and comp_nchan and sdant of the wrong type. The other 6 are noise levels just outside the suite's 5% band: tsys-manual interferometer noise 5.8% below CASA's recorded value, and tsys-atm single-dish noise 5.05% above it in all five variants. Those six are CASA's own seed-11111 draws, which casa-rs's random stream cannot reproduce; over 20 seeds the levels agree to 0.5% (noise-seeds-20261103). 23 cases fail with CASA's own task too and 16 are skipped by both. CASA's own simobserve suite (93 cases): sky models, component lists, both, noise, bad inputs and correlators, judged by the suite's checks against casatestdata's reference products.

#### smoothcal interacting modes and task behavior

##### Calibration table operation

**Implemented** — Time windows, selected fields, mean and median, complex phase tracking, real delays, flags, uncertainties, in-place updates and rate-aware fringe solutions. Includes saved table views, required scalar paths, blank selectors, boolean duration, staged spectral-window flags, and actively locked destination rejection. Linked control files are copied into an independent output snapshot.

The documented CASA behavior differences are recorded below.

Evidence: [paired](#smoothcal-evidence-paired).

#### smoothcal deviations and unfinished work

##### preserve-fringe-delay-units: Proposed

- Inputs: Fringe Jones smoothing with smoothtype set to median.
- CASA: Wraps delay and other non-phase values as radians and bypasses their median.
- casa-rs: Preserves their units and applies the numerical median to each non-phase series.
- Rationale: The source condition applies phase handling to every parameter. An 8 ns delay became about 1.717 ns.
- User impact: The fringe phase comparisons pass and the non-phase outputs follow independently calculated medians.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [paired](#smoothcal-evidence-paired).

- Rationale: The native writer maps the selected rows to the original table after preparing the column.
- User impact: One call matches the columns after the CASA retry, with unselected rows retaining the initialized values.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [bins](#statwt-evidence-bins).

| `vis` | `''` | `''`; `vis` → `vis` | Partial | Contract 38: a list of MeasurementSets images as one, as CASA's tclean images its vis list. Each is opened and surveyed with its own selectors. All inputs share one observation string. Other selectors take one per MeasurementSet or one for every input. MeasurementSets are ordered stably by its earliest MAIN TIME and visited as CASA visits its ms0, ms1, ... keys, as text (input_parameters.checkAndFixSelectionPars, mslisthelper.sort_mslist, imager_base.selectData); one selecting no sample is left out unless it is the first (SynthesisImagerVi2::selectData). The image's coordinates (obs date, telescope, phase centre, rest frequency, a cube's axis) come from CASA's msobj (buildCoordinateSystem): the first MeasurementSet, or for a cube or cubedata whose start is a frequency or velocity the last one whose selected band holds it (CAS-12877); a continuum band, and so the MFS and MT-MFS reference frequency, spans every one. A cube reads each other MeasurementSet's window where it reaches the cube, and one that does not reach it is read so its MODEL_DATA holds the zero prediction, as CASA writes it. Weighting density spans every MeasurementSet; datacolumn falls back to DATA per MeasurementSet; savemodel writes each one's MODEL_DATA (or virtual model). CASA's addwtspec, which adds WEIGHT_SPECTRUM to a listed MeasurementSet lacking it as a Vi/VB2 workaround, is not done: casa-rs reads each MeasurementSet's own weights, which that column copies, and never modifies its inputs. A row's spectral window and field are keyed among every MeasurementSet's, as if they were concatenated, so the mosaic keeps each one's beams (CASA's msId_spw, SimplePBConvFunc::convIndex) and a mosweight density each one's fields (VisImagingWeight's msId_field) apart; its dishes are every MeasurementSet's aperture classes (HetArrayConvFunc::findAntennaSizes). Refused with several MeasurementSets (#980): the awproject gridder (its catalog keys cells on the first MeasurementSet's frequencies), a moving phase centre, specmode cubesource, fitspw and a cube's per-channel density weighting. A cube with an unset start reads the band selected over every MeasurementSet, on the first one's channels (SynthesisParamsImage::buildCoordinateSystem). Each input keeps the field text. Only exactly empty text selects all fields without matching metadata. A blank token can match an empty name or code. A bare token such as none or -1 can be a field name. Quotes allow bracket and brace patterns and commas inside a term. Quoted patterns and slash regexes discard backslashes and newlines as the CASA scanner does. Names match unflagged stored NAMEs before CODEs. Pattern CODE matching uses the stored text, and literal NAME and CODE comparisons trim only spaces. In-range numeric IDs include flagged rows. Out-of-range IDs within the signed 32-bit domain can match the first unflagged decimal NAME or CODE over the catalogue. Overflow is refused (#54). Slash regexes support positive and negative lookahead with whole-string byte matching. Unsupported ECMAScript groups are refused (#54). Bare escapes are refused so the scanner cannot silently drop input and select different rows (CASA bug, #54). Literal dollar signs at FIELD token boundaries and regex end anchors are accepted in tclean. Environment and shell expressions are refused.
