#### tclean interacting modes and task behavior

<a id="tclean-behavior-selection"></a>
##### Selection and multi-MS inputs

**Partial** — vis, field, spw, timerange, uvrange, antenna, scan, observation, intent, datacolumn and selectdata (#54).

IDs/ranges, names/simple patterns, mixed field lists, SPW/channel text, intent and UV limits are routed natively. Sixteen field cases compare exact physical MAIN row order or refusal with CASA, including flagged and padded FIELD metadata. Since the main imaging cutover was integrated (3016f1b), FIELD selection resolves over the observation catalogue's FIELD rows on MSv2 and MSv4 alike; on the production traversal the field cases of the CASA row oracle (IDs, names, glob, mixed, range) and both refusals read exactly CASA's physical MAIN rows. Production T1 compares ID/name selections with selectdata=False on the single native route. Scan and observation selection is active from tclean contract 33 (owner decision 2026-11-02): on that path scan 1, scan 3 and observation 0 read exactly CASA's rows, and T1 images each numeric selection as its equivalent FIELD selection with either selectdata value and refuses CASA's refused forms without writing images. Through the public Python task, 13 science cases and 23 CASA grammar cases pass against CASA on CPU64, CPU32 and Metal32 (108/108). CODE/numeric-name fallback, advanced field forms, richer scan/observation grammar, remain unfinished; a vis list images as one observation from contract 38, as CASA's tclean does (awproject with several MeasurementSets is refused, #980); antenna and timerange are active from contract 34 (timerange on MeasurementSets only). Image-science comparisons for selected real datasets, flags, channel membership and data-column fallback remain separate required evidence.

Evidence: [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [representative](#tclean-evidence-representative), [field-selection](#tclean-evidence-field-selection), [cloud-continuation](#tclean-evidence-cloud-continuation), [scan-observation-activation](#tclean-evidence-scan-observation-activation), [vis-list-20261102](#tclean-evidence-vis-list-20261102).

<a id="tclean-behavior-restart"></a>
##### Restart, product persistence and recalculation

**Partial** — imagename, restart, startmodel, calcres, calcpsf, restoration; main and outlier fields (#944).

Contract 36 continues every spectral mode, Taylor family and Stokes set of the main image and activates calcres/calcpsf (CASA test-case matrix at 4fe0e56: 11/48 restart/calcres/calcpsf cases pass, from 1/48 counting the 74a3b85 run's CASA refusals as environment failures; the rest are blocked by other gaps or an f32 scalar floor). Earlier: paired CASA 6.7.6.14 small standard Stokes-I MFS defaults pass (18 native 10->0->10 rows, 6 persisted nontrivial-mask cases, 6 CASA-to-native and 2 native-to-CASA continuations). Embedded model/mask pixel masks, tabulated spectral grids, new explicit/auto masks over occupied masks when cleaning, other outlier and direction-dependent restart variants and faceted restarts remain unfinished. An ordinary natural-weighted flat-noise Stokes-I Högbom mosaic can continue from its saved PSF and residual with a user mask or restore them without cleaning in MFS and cubes (#944). A natural-weighted Stokes-I Högbom MFS run with outliers and user masks can rebuild each field's residual from its saved model while keeping that field's PSF, positive sum of weights and PB (#944). With both PSF and residual saved, the same fields use their own saved residual for the first CLEAN boundary and keep it when no major cycle runs. A PSF without a stored restoring beam can be fitted. With a new residual pass, a field’s zero or negative saved sum of weights is refilled from the pass while a previously positive sum is kept. A run starting with saved residuals still requires positive sums for all fields. Concurrency at one prefix remains unassessed. CASA mutates prior logtables whereas native preserves them (owner-agreed). New-image history completeness remains unfinished. This is not general persistence or full metadata acceptance.

Evidence: [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [lifecycle](#tclean-evidence-lifecycle), [restart-native-current](#tclean-evidence-restart-native-current), [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart), [scalars-empty-mask](#tclean-evidence-scalars-empty-mask), [numbering-preview](#tclean-evidence-numbering-preview), [numbering-activation](#tclean-evidence-numbering-activation), [continuation-20261102](#tclean-evidence-continuation-20261102).

<a id="tclean-behavior-spectral"></a>
##### Cube axes, reference frequencies and moving sources

**Partial** — specmode, spw, start, width, nchan, reffreq, restfreq, outframe, veltype, interpolation and perchanweightdensity.

nchan=-1 takes CASA's count from the start or the first selected channel to the band's far edge in channel, frequency and radio-velocity grids, and interpolation='cubic' fits casacore's four-point cubic (#1066); standard LSRK optical-velocity cubes preserve CASA's stored frequency table, extrapolate extra planes by its last interval, and match channel gridding, prediction, and density weights (#1096). The other optical gridder and frame combinations and a constant table on multiple image planes remain scoped out; a cube over several selected windows lays its axis over their channels merged as CASA's MSTransformRegridder::combineSpwsCore merges them, grids every window's rows onto it, and with nchan=-1 counts a channel grid's planes over the merged band as regridChanBounds does (#980); MFS outframe (LSRK/BARY/TOPO, header only, gridding stays LSRK as in CASA) and restfreq lists (first active, the others listed in the header) are read; MFS REST outframe and blank restfreq entries remain restricted. Moving-source cubesource needs its own representative oracle (#714). Fresh standard MVC uses cube major cycles and Taylor minor cycles. The standard multi-SPW dirty and clean comparisons pass, with remaining cases on #1069. The moving-MFS spectral envelope now uses CASA FIELD-origin direction semantics; six fixed/moving CPU64/CPU32/GPU32 comparisons pass recorded WCS values, and the previous 3.5 Hz increment mismatch is repaired at its unchanged tolerance. This does not complete moving-PB or cubesource acceptance. The ordinary MFS default SOURCE rest-frequency label is now repaired; five fresh mosaic/AW weight families and small restart metadata checks match. DOPPLER-backed SOURCE lookup and multiple SOURCE key groups with stored wildcards are explicitly unfinished, not approved deviations. The MFS header's first visibility field is the least (ARRAY_ID, DATA_DESC_ID, FIELD_ID) of the selected samples, CASA's buffer order: the MSv2 adapter states each partition's array and the survey reads the rows' arrays for a partition holding several (3bdf6fa, after Astra's review found the merge had dropped ARRAY_ID); a T1 run with opposing arrays records CASA's choice. An MSv4 has no arrays. The moving-MFS increment oracle on the catalogue path gives CASA's 125020996.11132812 Hz exactly (8b0fe44).

Evidence: [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [representative](#tclean-evidence-representative), [mvc-decision](#tclean-evidence-mvc-decision), [taylor-pb-mfs](#tclean-evidence-taylor-pb-mfs), [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart), [cloud-continuation](#tclean-evidence-cloud-continuation), [cube-axes-20261103](#tclean-evidence-cube-axes-20261103).

<a id="tclean-behavior-gridders"></a>
##### Gridder, weighting and beam combinations

**Partial** — Standard, W projection, mosaic, AW projection and bounded AWP2; geometry, facets, normalization, beam terms and density weighting.

AWP2’s single-field dirty, two-field clean with model-column write, nonzero-W continuum, squinted Stokes IV continuum, and line cubes with single-channel windows or nearest interpolation agree with CASA (#1071). The named unsquinted Stokes continuum and cube cases also agree. The two-term MFS case also agrees across both selected fields and three single-channel windows. The one-field natural flat-noise AWP2 cube-major-cycle case agrees on both cube and Taylor products. The named two-field, uniform-weighted Stokes I AWP2 case with squint and four W planes agrees with CASA when its sensitivity FFT uses double precision. The release CASA Float FFT can change four pixels at the primary-beam cutoff. The raw and controlled comparisons are recorded in the [CASA defect notes](../CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#awp2s-float-sensitivity-fft-can-flip-the-primary-beam-cutoff). Rectangular standard/W/mosaic and uvtaper were implemented in #970. AW remains square/equal-cell, and images MFS, MT-MFS and cubes whose selected windows hold one channel each; multi-channel cubes also run with nearest interpolation in the data, LSRK, tracked TOPO or tracked BARY frame, or from TOPO into the moving source REST frame with natural weighting (#1121), and linear interpolation between LSRK, tracked TOPO and tracked BARY with natural, Briggs or uniform weighting or from TOPO into moving source REST with natural weighting, and cubic interpolation between LSRK, tracked TOPO and tracked BARY with natural, Briggs or uniform weighting or from TOPO into moving source REST with natural weighting. The one-field cubic REST AW route also supports Briggs and uniform with per-channel density and no UV taper. The native TOPO data-frame route supports natural nearest, linear and cubic (each plane its own weight image, issue 719; remaining combinations wait for issue 1121); it reads tclean's aterm, psterm, wbawp, conjbeams and any positive wprojplanes (#980), and an imported CASA cache must already exist: where cfcache names a missing directory CASA fills it, casa-rs refuses (aw_cf_source=native-evla generates its own). The imported two-field `test_mosaic_mtmfs` caches agree with CASA for both beam choices, including pointing with uniformly odd cache buffers (#1214, #1070). Mixed-parity caches use each selected buffer's own pointing origin, avoiding CASA's reuse of a wider gradient array (#1070). On same-prefix continuation CASA can multiply the saved higher Taylor weight planes again. casa-rs recomputes the weights with the PSF and agrees with fresh CASA controls (#1315, #1070). Continuation with `calcpsf=False,calcres=True` reuses the saved AW PSF and weights (#1317); two-term PB correction is also supported in this case (#1318). Mosaic per-field density weighting (mosweight) is implemented, continuum and a cube's per-channel density (BriggsCubeWeightor multiField, #818); W/AW facets and additional gridders/weightings remain incomplete. Native CF generation is verified separately from CASA cache oracles. The native write_pb default is True. Homogeneous ALMA-labelled 7m arrays select ACA; legacy VLA PB now covers all named bands and NVSS frequency gaps. Fresh ordinary-default W/Hogbom20 CPU64/CPU32 runs pass all seven products, with PB NRMS zero. EVLA/VLA mosaics grid with CASA's common EVLA primary beam (HetArrayConvFunc COMMONPB, PBMath1DEVLA) at the first buffer's LSRK frequencies and MosaicFT's sector edges; conjbeams on one-plane mosaics grids with CASA's widened, resampled conjugate cell (#980). Moving/nonconstant FIELD directions, mixed dish classes, unsupported telescopes and remaining EVLA bands are unfinished. Explicit GPU W/AW remains refused. CASA Float channel-frequency narrowing is now matched in shared Taylor factors. All five fresh mosaic/native-AW MT-MFS rows pass the owner-approved scoped weak weight.tt1 rule and retained original recorded checks; 3 override only raw weight.tt1 relative-error failures. Exact guards and 1e-6 matrix-scale limits remain. Full metadata is separate. Existing #690 odd-sumwt scaling remains distinct. Legacy VLA cube PB takes CASA's channel-zero aperture scaled per channel: both T1.5 VLA cube rows give .pb NRMS 0.0 at 9768bb1, 3016f1b and 2628d8b (pre-candidate 0.0136); independent review pending. Cube Briggs density cells now use CASA's negated u and v (2628d8b): all 3,056,967 point-cube-briggs (row, channel) weights match CASA's to 1.35e-7, where 7 exact Float ties previously read a neighbouring cell.

Evidence: [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [additions](#tclean-evidence-additions), [representative](#tclean-evidence-representative), [default-products](#tclean-evidence-default-products), [compensated-current](#tclean-evidence-compensated-current), [taylor-pb-mfs](#tclean-evidence-taylor-pb-mfs), [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart), [cloud-continuation](#tclean-evidence-cloud-continuation), [awp2-dirty-mfs](#tclean-evidence-awp2-dirty-mfs).

**Partial** — Hogbom, Clark, Clark-Stokes, multiscale, MT-MFS, iteration controls, user masks and auto-multithresh.

Clark-Stokes uses Clark's solver on each polarization separately, while Clark jointly selects and updates a channel's polarization planes (#1126). General regions and other mask combinations remain unfinished. #### tclean deviations and unfinished work

##### interactive-headless: Agreed for now

- Inputs: interactive=True; graphical mask editing and pause/resume.
- CASA: Uses casaviewer where available; 6.7.6.14 on macOS raises when the viewer is absent.
- casa-rs: Refuses interactive=True explicitly; accepts False. Supply a mask or use supported auto-multithresh controls.
- Rationale: The application is headless; the owner accepted the exception for the current phase.
- User impact: No graphical mask editing/pause-resume. Future interactive operation remains wanted, not permanently out of scope.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Headless exception for now, but ultimately we will want to do something for this. Recorded on #980.
- Evidence: [interactive-decision](#tclean-evidence-interactive-decision), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader).

##### mvc: Unfinished

- Inputs: specmode='mvc'.
- CASA: Supports the MVC task path.
- casa-rs: Supports the bounded fresh standard-gridder mode and same-prefix CLEAN with two supplied Taylor start models. Explicit Taylor start models use the saved cube and Taylor primary beams to project the first cube model. An ordinary restart reads the saved cube model for prediction and the saved Taylor terms for the solver. The three-SPW dirty, clean, PB-corrected and seeded clean references agree on all published images, masks, coordinates and controller counts. The original flat-noise mosaic case also agrees for dirty imaging and a ten-iteration clean, including the common-beam correction of both Taylor images. The original four-plane W-projection dirty and cleaned cases agree on both product families and controller counts. The original flat-noise AW-projection case also agrees with imported or natively generated cube caches, including both PB-corrected Taylor images.
- Rationale: The Taylor header spans the first and last published cube channel centres and preserves the cube rest-frequency label. The polynomial expansion has its own reference frequency.
- User impact: Other continuation modes and additional gridders remain on #1069. The separate dirty alpha case agrees with CASA after correcting its standard-grid sector bounds.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [mvc-decision](#tclean-evidence-mvc-decision), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader).

##### restart: Unfinished

- Inputs: Any occupied main/outlier image namespace; restart=False or recalculation controls.
- CASA: Continues existing products by default, or chooses a numbered fresh prefix with restart=False.
- casa-rs: Bounded same-grid standard Stokes-I MFS default continuation now has native gates, small paired CASA 10->0->10/mask evidence and both-direction continuation. Contract32 activates single-main fresh numbering; small public products/preservation pass. Other occupied namespaces, coordinated outlier/orphan numbering and calc flags remain unfinished.
- Rationale: Reuse the existing native model/mask lifecycle with admitted ownership, preserving unsupported-state refusals while completing parity.
- User impact: The bounded native default path can continue prior work; unsupported modes and flags still require completion and are not agreed exclusions.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [lifecycle](#tclean-evidence-lifecycle), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [restart-native-current](#tclean-evidence-restart-native-current), [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart), [numbering-activation](#tclean-evidence-numbering-activation).

##### uvtaper-units: Previously agreed

- Inputs: A unitless uvtaper entry.
- CASA: Interprets bare values as radians, despite documenting lambda; large values may zero every imaging weight.
- casa-rs: Requires explicit angle or lambda/klambda units and errors clearly on bare values.
- Rationale: Prevent a documented-unit mismatch from silently producing an empty image.
- User impact: Callers must supply units; numerical unit-bearing taper behavior remains governed by #970 evidence.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Require explicit units.
- Evidence: [additions](#tclean-evidence-additions), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader).

##### startmodel-stokes: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Start-model Stokes labels differ from the target; equal plane counts.
- CASA: Copies planes by position without converting polarization, since only direction and spectral axes are regridded.
- casa-rs: Copies equal-count planes by position and warns; focused native warning/permuted-plane tests pass, and the single Q-to-I case is paired with CASA 6.7.6.14. Multi-plane paired and unequal-count behavior remain unverified.
- Rationale: Match CASA's behavior, while making the label mismatch visible.
- User impact: A Q model can seed I and permuted Stokes planes are copied positionally; this is not a physical polarization conversion. Unequal-plane-count behavior still needs oracle assessment.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Match but issue a warning. This supersedes the prior refusal.
- Evidence: [additions](#tclean-evidence-additions), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader), [default-products](#tclean-evidence-default-products).

##### restart-absolute-directory: Previously agreed

- Inputs: restart=False with an absolute imagename and existing products.
- CASA: 6.7.6.14 incrementImageNameList slices dirname[2:], corrupting an absolute directory before creating the next numbered image; the probe fails to create its PSF.
- casa-rs: Activated native contract32 keeps the correct absolute directory; alternating absolute/relative public calls choose and publish the expected fresh prefixes.
- Rationale: Avoid a reproducible CASA path-handling bug while preserving the intended numbering behavior.
- User impact: Numbered products stay in the requested directory. Broader restart acceptance remains open.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Use the correct absolute directory. Recorded on #944.
- Evidence: [lifecycle](#tclean-evidence-lifecycle), [numbering-preview](#tclean-evidence-numbering-preview), [numbering-activation](#tclean-evidence-numbering-activation).

##### native-write-pb-default: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Ordinary casa-rs tclean calls that omit the casa-rs-only write_pb option; profiles from contract 29 or earlier.
- CASA: Ordinary supported tclean imaging creates a .pb product; CASA has no write_pb parameter.
- casa-rs: Contract 30 defaults the extra write_pb option to True. Explicit False remains an opt-out; migrating an omitted old default warns and adopts True. All 92 CASA parameters/defaults and pbcor=False are unchanged.
- Rationale: Make ordinary product production agree with CASA without patching CASA or changing its parameter defaults.
- User impact: The PB file is now produced within implemented PB scope. Moving-field, telescope and frequency limitations remain unfinished work and can currently require explicit False.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Approve the casa-rs default change.
- Evidence: [default-products](#tclean-evidence-default-products), [reader](#tclean-evidence-reader).

##### hogbom-default: Previously agreed

- Inputs: deconvolver='hogbom' with a positive minor-cycle iteration limit.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 may commit one extra component while clamping its reported count to the requested limit.
- casa-rs: Contract31 defaults the native extra policy to casa-inclusive; explicit strict remains available. Omitted older profile defaults warn and adopt the new value, while explicit values are preserved.
- Rationale: Match CASA's reported count and scientific products using the existing implementation.
- User impact: Positive Hogbom cycles may apply one extra component while reporting the CASA count. Other solvers retain their canonical strict inactive policy. No CASA parameter/default changes.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-31, this chat: Approved both proposed adoptions, including CASA-compatible Hogbom counting by default.
- Evidence: [compensated-current](#tclean-evidence-compensated-current), [adopted-defaults](#tclean-evidence-adopted-defaults).

##### weak-taylor-weight-comparison: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Two-term Stokes-I MFS mosaic/AW weight.tt1; both reference weak-coupling measures<=1e-3, with all reviewed accumulator guards.
- CASA: An almost cancelling odd weight term makes error relative to its own near-zero norm unstable; exact CASA product values remain the oracle.
- casa-rs: The approved gate uses E2 across valid pixels and Emax on reference-only PB support, each<=1e-6 of the Taylor matrix scale. All other original checks remain. Three raw NRMS failures are visible scoped overrides; outputs are unchanged.
- Rationale: Judge a weak coupling against its surrounding positive Taylor matrix while preserving PSD, masks, finiteness and other scientific checks.
- User impact: An odd term below the matrix-scale error budget could be lost and still pass this one criterion. No model, metadata or arbitrary-mode waiver.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-11-01, this chat: Approve the scoped comparison rule.
- Evidence: [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart).

##### specific-weak-mtmfs-model-output: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Only original b6a87 clean8/cpu32 512-square standard MT-MFS result bound by the owner-decision receipt and payload identities.
- CASA: The weak model.tt1 coefficient is -0.00026645659818314016 Jy; the original raw comparison remains available.
- casa-rs: The bound coefficient is -0.0002667965891305357 Jy, raw NRMS 0.0012759712. The owner accepted this exact output: ideal published intensity differs by at most 5.7469e-7 in the recorded common-frame MFS interval, with all 18 other original product checks passing.
- Rationale: A mathematically checked component solve and exact support show that this specific coefficient discrepancy has a much smaller represented in-band intensity effect.
- User impact: The raw failure remains; this exact reviewed output is accepted. Future outputs have no automatic approval, and runtime visibility prediction remains separately unverified.
- Owner decision: Owner, 2026-11-01, this chat: Accept this specific reviewed output.
- Evidence: [standard-mtmfs-current](#tclean-evidence-standard-mtmfs-current), [approved-comparisons-restart](#tclean-evidence-approved-comparisons-restart).

##### numbering-metal-cyclethreshold: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Only unchanged99b cli-gpu32/explicit_startmodel output and bound raw receipt/input/binary identities.
- CASA: Final cyclethreshold0.07878141850233078 Jy/beam.
- casa-rs: 0.07878153771162033 Jy/beam; raw original scalar comparison fails by1.5132ppm. Formula matches measured native state; upstream residual cause unproved.
- Rationale: Owner accepted this exact output under2e-6 relative+1e-8 Jy/beam with all other recorded checks retained; engineering choice, not a universal Float error bound.
- User impact: Accepts0.119209microJy/beam in this returned threshold only; changes no values/defaults/algorithm and grants no future-output waiver.
- Owner decision: Owner2026-11-01, this chat: Accept this specific output. Raw failed verdict retained.
- Evidence: [numbering-activation](#tclean-evidence-numbering-activation).

##### numbered-prior-history: Previously agreed

- Inputs: restart=False fresh numbered outputs with older matching-prefix images.
- CASA: Appends later task history to all old matching image logtables; paired runs change only old logtable/table.dat and table.f0.
- casa-rs: Leaves old files unchanged byte for byte, excluding locks.
- Rationale: The owner agreed preserving independent older results instead of appending history from later fresh-numbering calls.
- User impact: Old histories omit later calls creating other images. Correct history on each new image remains required and unassessed.
- Owner decision: Owner2026-11-01, this chat: Preserve prior histories. Correct new-image history is not waived.
- Evidence: [numbering-activation](#tclean-evidence-numbering-activation).

#### wvrgcal deviations and unfinished work

##### sparse-window-phase-reversal: Previously agreed

- Record: [WVR global phase reversal can miss sparse spectral-window selections](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/e7aad96dc5f350765fa5130e1faf10a1f10da121/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#wvr-global-phase-reversal-can-miss-sparse-spectral-window-selections)
- Inputs: A direct wvr.gcal invocation with global phase reversal and a sparse spectral-window selection.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 can leave selected windows unchanged when the selected position differs from the actual ID.
- casa-rs: Reverse the phase of every selected spectral-window ID.
- Rationale: Match the documented phase operation and the algebraic conjugation of the ordinary gains.
- User impact: A sparse output selection produces the same reversed phases as the corresponding subset of an all-window reversal.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [parameter-options](#wvrgcal-evidence-parameter-options).

##### wvr-failed-segment-assignment: Proposed

- Record: [WVR can move successful atmospheric fits into earlier segments](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/e7aad96dc5f350765fa5130e1faf10a1f10da121/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#wvr-can-move-successful-atmospheric-fits-into-earlier-segments)
- Inputs: Run the default segmented WVR retrieval on the pinned recorded ALMA observation.
- CASA: Two successful fits take the first two time bounds after two other fits fail.
- casa-rs: Keep each successful fit attached to its original observation segment.
- Rationale: The retrieved atmospheric coefficients describe conditions in those segments.
- User impact: Each calibration gain is evaluated against the corresponding atmospheric fit.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [recorded-alma](#wvrgcal-evidence-recorded-alma).

##### wvr-empty-retrieval: Proposed

- Record: [WVR can dereference a missing single retrieval](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/e7aad96dc5f350765fa5130e1faf10a1f10da121/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#wvr-can-dereference-a-missing-single-retrieval)
- Inputs: Request one fixed-interval retrieval and a negative one-second offset on the pinned observation.
- CASA: The pinned CASA process exits with SIGSEGV after a failed-reference retry.
- casa-rs: Return a failed retrieval without publishing a calibration table.
- Rationale: A flagged or rejected fit leaves no coefficients to apply.
- User impact: The caller can choose other intervals or a suitable reference antenna and retry.
- Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
- Evidence: [recorded-alma](#wvrgcal-evidence-recorded-alma).

### componentlist

#### componentlist method implementation

Implementation status is **not behavioral verification**. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing modes or combinations, which raise `NotImplementedError` naming the issue shown; Not implemented raises it for every call; Disabled in CASA and Deprecated in CASA do what CASA does; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below.

Audit baseline: `69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e`. Status counts: Implemented: 61, Partial: 0, Not implemented: 0, Disabled in CASA: 0, Deprecated in CASA: 0, Unassessed: 0.

#### componentlist interacting modes and tool behavior

#### componentlist deviations and unfinished work

##### limb-darkened-disk-no-exponent: Previously agreed

- Record: [Writing a limb-darkened disk without an exponent aborts CASA](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#writing-a-limb-darkened-disk-without-an-exponent-aborts-casa)
- Inputs: cl.fromrecord for a limb-darkened disk without optionalParameters, then cl.close.
- CASA: writeTable stores an empty optional-parameter vector and throws casacore::indexError from the ComponentList destructor, terminating the process (CASA 6.7.6: close aborts); readTable would read out of bounds.
- casa-rs: Leaves the cell undefined, read as the shape's default exponent 0.05.
- Rationale: The default exponent is what every undescribed row already reads as.
- User impact: Such lists save and reload instead of aborting the process.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### single-spectral-index-read-past-end: Previously agreed

- Record: [A single spectral index is read past its end](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#a-single-spectral-index-is-read-past-its-end)
- Inputs: cl.addcomponent(spectrumtype='spectral index', index=alpha) on a polarised component, then predict.
- CASA: The matrix sampleStokes used by every component prediction has no one-index branch and reads indices 1 to 3 out of bounds; the per-frequency version scales only I (read from source, not probed).
- casa-rs: Reads a single index as [alpha,0,0,0], so fractional polarisation is constant.
- Rationale: This is what the matrix sampler's comments describe.
- User impact: Polarised components with one index predict Q, U, V reliably instead of scaled by whatever follows the vector.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### addcomponent-four-flux-as-stokes: Previously agreed

- Record: [`cl.addcomponent` stores four flux values as Stokes](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#claddcomponent-stores-four-flux-values-as-stokes)
- Inputs: cl.addcomponent(flux=[1,0.1,0.2,0.9], polarization='circular').
- CASA: setflux stores four values with FluxRep::setValue(Vector<Double>), which resets the representation to Stokes, so the values become I,Q,U,V rather than RR,RL,LR,LL (probed with CASA 6.7.6).
- casa-rs: Does the same (owner decision 2026-10-23), including raising for an unknown name or a non-Stokes representation with one value.
- Rationale: Scripts get the list CASA would give them.
- User impact: A circular or linear four-value flux is silently read as Stokes in both implementations.
- Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-23 (#841), recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### addcomponent-flux-single-precision: Previously agreed

- Record: [`cl.addcomponent` stores the flux in single precision](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#claddcomponent-stores-the-flux-in-single-precision)
- Inputs: cl.addcomponent(flux=0.1).
- CASA: setflux reads values into a Vector<Complex> (single precision), so flux=0.1 is stored as 0.10000000149011612 (CASA 6.7.6).
- casa-rs: Keeps the values given.
- Rationale: Avoids a needless single-precision rounding.
- User impact: Fluxes differ from CASA's by at most 6e-8 relative.
- Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### addcomponent-point-for-bad-shape: Previously agreed

- Record: [`cl.addcomponent` keeps a point for a shape it cannot make](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/69aa2b7091d025b82edc539b51a17535e075ae0e/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#claddcomponent-keeps-a-point-for-a-shape-it-cannot-make)
- Inputs: cl.addcomponent with a misspelled shape name, a limb-darkened disk, or an axis that is not an angle.
- CASA: addcomponent ignores setshape's False return, so the component stays a point and addcomponent returns True (CASA 6.7.6).
- casa-rs: Does the same and logs at ERROR; what setshape raises, addcomponent raises too after removing the component.
- Rationale: Scripts that misspell a shape get points, as in CASA.
- User impact: A misspelled shape yields a point source instead of an error.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### isphysical-empty-list-exit: Previously agreed

- Inputs: componentlist().isphysical(), default [-1] selection on an empty list.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6-14 exits the Python process without raising an exception.
- casa-rs: Raises a catchable RuntimeError; an explicit empty index list still returns True.
- Rationale: A component check should not terminate its caller.
- User impact: Callers can recover rather than lose the Python session.
- Owner decision: Owner approved a catchable error on 2026-11-05 (#1158).
- Evidence: [isphysical-casa](#componentlist-evidence-isphysical-casa).

##### iscomponentlist-cyclic-input: Previously agreed

- Inputs: A self-referential Python list passed to componentlist.iscomponentlist.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6-14 terminates the Python process with SIGSEGV.
- casa-rs: Logs the placeholder warning and returns False without recursing forever.
- Rationale: A type-check placeholder should not terminate its caller.
- User impact: Callers retain the Python session.
- Owner decision: Owner approved correcting CASA crashes as a class on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
- Evidence: [iscomponentlist-casa](#componentlist-evidence-iscomponentlist-casa).

##### missing-flux-polarisation-default: Previously agreed

- Inputs: cl.add(record) omits flux.polarisation and flux.error.
- CASA: Warns that the default is Stokes but writes Unknown.
- casa-rs: Uses the announced Stokes default.
- Rationale: Correct the contradiction of the stated default and valid component intent.
- User impact: Imported components remain usable and serializable with Stokes flux.
- Owner decision: Standing AGENTS.md CASA-deviations rule: correct crashes and contradictions of documentation or evident intent.
- Evidence: [record-import-casa](#componentlist-evidence-record-import-casa), [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

##### invalid-gaussian-record-abort: Previously agreed

- Inputs: Gaussian record imports with non-positive axes, minor greater than major, or position angle outside ±360 degrees.
- CASA: Aborts the process from GaussianShape constructor assertions.
- casa-rs: Raises a catchable RuntimeError before appending.
- Rationale: Correct a CASA process abort under the standing crash-correction rule.
- User impact: The existing list and Python session remain available.
- Owner decision: Standing AGENTS.md CASA-deviations rule: correct crashes and contradictions of documentation or evident intent.
- Evidence: [record-import-casa](#componentlist-evidence-record-import-casa), [bugs-record](#componentlist-evidence-bugs-record).

### measures

#### measures method implementation

Implementation status is **not behavioral verification**. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing modes or combinations, which raise `NotImplementedError` naming the issue shown; Not implemented raises it for every call; Disabled in CASA and Deprecated in CASA do what CASA does; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below.

Audit baseline: `5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f`. Status counts: Implemented: 48, Partial: 0, Not implemented: 0, Disabled in CASA: 0, Deprecated in CASA: 0, Unassessed: 0.

#### measures interacting modes and tool behavior

#### measures deviations and unfinished work

##### measures-tool-default-frame: Previously agreed

- Record: [The measures tool converts with a frame at MJD 0 and the geocentre](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#the-measures-tool-converts-with-a-frame-at-mjd-0-and-the-geocentre)
- Inputs: me.measure(me.direction('J2000','12h00m00','45d00m00'),'AZEL') in a fresh measures tool, with no doframe call.
- CASA: The tool starts with a default frame (MJD 0 UTC, zero-vector position, J2000 pole) and converts using it without a warning, returning AZEL for 1858-11-17 at the Earth's centre.
- casa-rs: Starts with an empty frame, so the conversion fails with 'Cannot convert due to missing frame information' until doframe sets the element.
- Rationale: A conversion should not silently use placeholder epoch and position.
- User impact: A script that forgot doframe gets an error rather than a meaningless answer.
- Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### iau2000-keeps-iau1980-sidereal: Previously agreed

- Record: [IAU 2000 keeps the IAU 1980 sidereal time and ecliptic obliquities](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#iau-2000-keeps-the-iau-1980-sidereal-time-and-ecliptic-obliquities)
- Inputs: Conversions to HADEC, AZEL, ITRF, MECLIPTIC or TECLIPTIC with measures.iau2000.b_use set.
- CASA: casacore still forms GAST from IAU 1982 GMST and the IAU 1980 equation of the equinoxes, and uses IAU 1980 obliquities (fundArg T^2 term -0.0059 arcsec, 0.37 mas in MECLIPTIC by 2026).
- casa-rs: Computes all of these as casacore does (casacore_sidereal, casacore_frames).
- Rationale: Follows casacore for parity; it moved IAU 2000A J2000 to HADEC from 20.4 to 16.7 mas off casacore.
- User impact: Results under IAU 2000 match casacore, including its remaining IAU 1980 pieces.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### direction-latitude-unnormalized: Previously agreed

- Record: [Direction latitudes come from an unnormalized vector](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#direction-latitudes-come-from-an-unnormalized-vector)
- Inputs: Direction conversions that use the galactic or FK4 matrices, e.g. B1950 to GALACTIC or J2000 to B1950 near a pole.
- CASA: The 10-digit literal matrices are orthogonal only to about 7e-11 and doConvert does not renormalize, so getLat's asin(z) is off by (|v|-1)tan(b) and becomes NaN once z exceeds 1.
- casa-rs: Converts with the same matrices, renormalizes and reports the latitude of the unit vector.
- Rationale: asin(z) assumes a unit vector.
- User impact: Reported angles differ by up to 51 microarcsec (1.6 mas at b=-89.77 deg) while directions agree to 0.01 microarcsec.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### iau2000-jmean-j2000-order: Previously agreed

- Record: [IAU 2000 JMEAN to J2000 applies bias and precession in the wrong order](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#iau-2000-jmean-to-j2000-applies-bias-and-precession-in-the-wrong-order)
- Inputs: MECLIPTIC or TECLIPTIC to J2000 conversion under IAU 2000.
- CASA: deapplyPrecession applies B then P giving P*B*v', not the inverse B*P*v', so JMEAN to J2000 is not the inverse of J2000 to JMEAN (0.14 mas off in 2026, growing).
- casa-rs: Inverts exactly.
- Rationale: The reverse transform must invert the forward one.
- User impact: Round trips through the IAU 2000 ecliptics differ from casacore by 0.14 mas in 2026.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### iau2000-gmst1-tt-fraction: Previously agreed

- Record: [IAU 2000 GMST1 adds the TT day fraction](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#iau-2000-gmst1-adds-the-tt-day-fraction)
- Inputs: UT1 to GMST1 (and so LMST) under IAU 2000.
- CASA: UT1_GMST1 adds GMST00/(2pi), already a sidereal time of day, to the TT epoch, counting the TT day fraction twice: UT1 51544.5 gives GMST1 58258.280 against 58257.779, and GMST1_UT1 does not undo it.
- casa-rs: Uses the IAU 1976 GMST1 under either model, as casacore's own GAST does.
- Rationale: This keeps GMST1, LMST, GAST and LAST consistent with each other.
- User impact: LMST differs from casacore's IAU 2000 value but agrees with casacore under IAU 1976.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### spectral-vector-data-loss: Previously agreed

- Record: [Measures spectral conversions reject or truncate valid vectors](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#measures-spectral-conversions-reject-or-truncate-valid-vectors)
- Inputs: Frequency/Doppler vectors passed to spectral helpers; cyclic list/dictionary arguments passed to doppler or todoppler.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 truncates tofrequency, toradialvelocity and torestfrequency vectors, rejects a valid unframed todoppler frequency vector, and terminates with SIGSEGV on the recorded cyclic arguments.
- casa-rs: Preserves every scalar-control result with scalar broadcasting; rejects cyclic/deep inputs with catchable ValueError and restores capture state after failure.
- Rationale: Correct scientific data loss, process crashes and behavior contradicting the scalar helper intent.
- User impact: Vector callers receive all requested results. Invalid cyclic arguments no longer terminate the process.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct CASA crashes, data loss and contradictions of evident intent.
- Evidence: [spectral-casa](#measures-evidence-spectral-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### geometry-unit-offset-loss: Previously agreed

- Record: [Measures geometry constructors lose values and mislabel units](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#measures-geometry-constructors-lose-values-and-mislabel-units)
- Inputs: Length-first baseline/UVW quantities, incompatible dimensions, valid UVW reference offsets and spherical magnetic fields.
- CASA: Can replace valid geometry with zero, discard the UVW offset, or mislabel tesla as nanotesla and magnetic extra values as metres.
- casa-rs: Retains geometry and its reference origin, checks dimensions, and returns magnetic components in nanotesla.
- Rationale: The angle-first constructor, generic measure offset and explicit Cartesian magnetic records supply independent controls for data and unit corruption.
- User impact: Geometry and magnetic field strengths are preserved with consistent units.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct data loss, corruption and contradictions of evident intent.
- Evidence: [geometry-casa](#measures-evidence-geometry-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### geometry-stale-auxiliary-results: Previously agreed

- Record: [Failed measures geometry calls can expose earlier outputs](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#failed-measures-geometry-calls-can-expose-earlier-outputs)
- Inputs: Failed touvw or expand following a successful call, and expand with an incompatible magnetic measure.
- CASA: Can return stale auxiliary results or relabel an incompatible record with zero length coordinates.
- casa-rs: Returns empty records for all outputs on failure and refuses non-geometric expansion.
- Rationale: Auxiliary values must correspond to the requested inputs.
- User impact: Callers can identify missing or incompatible results from all outputs.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct data loss, corruption and contradictions of evident intent.
- Evidence: [geometry-casa](#measures-evidence-geometry-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### geometry-magnetic-strength: Previously agreed

- Record: [Magnetic reference changes can corrupt field strength](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#magnetic-reference-changes-can-corrupt-field-strength)
- Inputs: Physical-strength fields transformed through diurnal aberration or directly between B1950 and APP.
- CASA: Changes field strength. For 37416.574 nT in B1950, the APP result has norm 22289.454 nT. A physical-strength reverse input produces NaNs.
- casa-rs: Uses the casacore conversion route on a unit vector, then restores the original field strength.
- Rationale: Direction corrections should leave field strength invariant. Independent CASA direction conversions supply the control.
- User impact: Corrects the changed magnitudes and finite-input NaNs.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct data loss, corruption and contradictions of evident intent.
- Evidence: [geometry-casa](#measures-evidence-geometry-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### comet-missing-epoch-crash: Previously agreed

- Record: [Comet numeric queries can terminate without an epoch](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#comet-numeric-queries-can-terminate-without-an-epoch)
- Inputs: A loaded comet table followed by cometdist or cometangdiam without setting an epoch, including after done.
- CASA: Terminates with SIGSEGV.
- casa-rs: Reports the missing epoch and returns the existing -1 AU or -1 rad missing-data sentinel.
- Rationale: A missing input frame element must not terminate the caller.
- User impact: Callers can set an epoch and retry using the same table.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct crashes and keep the approved empty initial frame.
- Evidence: [comet-casa](#measures-evidence-comet-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### shift-longitude-quadrant: Previously agreed

- Record: [Direction shifts can use the wrong longitude quadrant](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#direction-shifts-can-use-the-wrong-longitude-quadrant)
- Inputs: Angular direction offsets crossing a pole or reaching the other longitude quadrant.
- CASA: The inverse sine restricts longitude to the near quadrant. A 120-degree east shift moves 60 degrees, and a northward shift across the pole can leave the direction unchanged.
- casa-rs: Selects the longitude quadrant from both tangent-plane components. Retains the CASA convention when the input itself is exactly at a pole.
- Rationale: The documented operation gives a direction at the requested angular separation and position angle.
- User impact: Produces the intended separation and position angle for valid large shifts and pole crossings.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct results contradicting the documented operation.
- Evidence: [shift-casa](#measures-evidence-shift-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### showframe-lsr-context: Previously agreed

- Record: [Frame display can discard the coordinate conversion context](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#frame-display-can-discard-the-coordinate-conversion-context)
- Inputs: A configured frame and a velocity reference requiring conversion to LSRK or a LAST/LMST epoch.
- CASA: Reports an absent epoch, direction or position after all required frame elements have been set.
- casa-rs: Converts the displayed velocity to LSRK and the displayed epochs to TDB, UT1 and TT with the explicit frame.
- Rationale: Direct CASA measure conversions on the same inputs demonstrate the displayed results.
- User impact: The complete frame remains displayable for the seven affected velocity references and for LAST and LMST epochs.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct behavior contradicting documented intent.
- Evidence: [showframe-casa](#measures-evidence-showframe-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### showframe-missing-ut1: Previously agreed

- Record: [Frame display can report UT1 outside the Earth-orientation table](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#frame-display-can-report-ut1-outside-the-earth-orientation-table)
- Inputs: A frame epoch outside the supplied Earth-orientation coverage.
- CASA: Displays a numerical UT1 value after falling back to reduced-precision results.
- casa-rs: Marks UT1 unavailable and retains the raw epoch and available time scales.
- Rationale: A display should identify unavailable Earth-orientation measurements.
- User impact: The epoch stays visible after framenow and no unsupported UT1 value is presented.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct behavior contradicting documented intent.
- Evidence: [showframe-casa](#measures-evidence-showframe-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

##### comet-frame-refresh: Previously agreed

- Record: [Replacing a comet table can leave the previous frame direction cached](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/5b2b19bbb6c0549c44353ac119aa5c09b255211f/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#replacing-a-comet-table-can-leave-the-previous-frame-direction-cached)
- Inputs: Show or project the COMET frame direction, then replace the B1950 table with a TOPO table at ALMA.
- CASA: Direct COMET conversion updates immediately. Frame display and GEO to TOPO velocity can keep the previous position until the direction is reattached.
- casa-rs: The new table invalidates the displayed frame and updates the direction used for its projections.
- Rationale: A successful framecomet call replaces the active table. The fixture matches CASA after explicitly reattaching the direction.
- User impact: Frame display and Doppler projections update together after a successful ephemeris replacement.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: correct behavior contradicting documented intent.
- Evidence: [comet-direction-casa](#measures-evidence-comet-direction-casa), [bugs-record](#measures-evidence-bugs-record).

### quanta

#### quanta method implementation

Implementation status is **not behavioral verification**. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing modes or combinations, which raise `NotImplementedError` naming the issue shown; Not implemented raises it for every call; Disabled in CASA and Deprecated in CASA do what CASA does; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below.

Audit baseline: `ea0ad2a5158f77c82e5ab3681ef63ab264fb9332`. Status counts: Implemented: 57, Partial: 0, Not implemented: 0, Disabled in CASA: 0, Deprecated in CASA: 0, Unassessed: 0.

| CASA method | CASA parameters | Implementation | Scope | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `abs` | `v=[]` | Implemented | Arithmetic on quantities and arrays, with CASA's unit rules; arrays stay arrays. | [signature](#quanta-evidence-signature), [casa-values](#quanta-evidence-casa-values) |
| `acos` | `v=[]` | Implemented | Scalar trigonometry with CASA unit checking, quantity conversion errors and result units. | [signature](#quanta-evidence-signature), [trigonometry-casa](#quanta-evidence-trigonometry-casa) |
| `add` | `v=[], a=[]` | Implemented | Arithmetic on quantities and arrays, with CASA's unit rules; arrays stay arrays. | [signature](#quanta-evidence-signature), [casa-values](#quanta-evidence-casa-values), [record-complex-scalar-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-complex-scalar-casa), [record-complex-array-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-complex-array-casa), [bare-complex-scalar-casa](#quanta-evidence-bare-complex-scalar-casa), [record-empty-float-vector-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-empty-float-vector-casa), [record-zero-dimensional-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-zero-dimensional-casa), [record-sequence-edges-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-sequence-edges-casa) |

#### quanta interacting modes and tool behavior

#### quanta deviations and unfinished work

##### quantities-non-conforming-units: Previously agreed

- Record: [The tools convert quantities whose units do not conform](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/ea0ad2a5158f77c82e5ab3681ef63ab264fb9332/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#the-tools-convert-quantities-whose-units-do-not-conform)
- Inputs: integrationtime='10Jy', integrationtime='10m' or freq='1s' passed to a simulator method; a direction string such as 'J2000 12h00m00 garbage'.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6 converts without checking conformance: '10Jy' becomes 1e-25 s, '10m' 10 s, '1s' 1 Hz, and an unreadable direction token keeps the previous value (declination 180 deg).
- casa-rs: Refuses both with casacore's 'From/to units not consistent' or a parse error, while keeping CASA's cross-dimension conversions (number is SI, angle is time, length is frequency via c).
- Rationale: Non-conforming units are almost certainly user errors and should not become silent wrong values.
- User impact: Scripts with a wrong unit now stop with an error instead of running with a nonsense value.
- Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
- Evidence: [bugs-record](#quanta-evidence-bugs-record).

##### quanta-discarded-numpy-scalar-sequences: Previously agreed

- Record: [CASA drops NumPy scalars from mixed quantity-record sequences](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/ea0ad2a5158f77c82e5ab3681ef63ab264fb9332/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#casa-drops-numpy-scalars-from-mixed-quantity-record-sequences)
- Inputs: Quantity-record lists or tuples with unsigned NumPy integer scalars or NumPy booleans, or mixed boolean/numeric sequences with NumPy timedeltas or longlong scalars.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 discards those members when it builds the record, sometimes returning a shortened scalar or vector.
- casa-rs: Reject such quantity records before parsing the unit or running the quantity operation.
- Rationale: Preserve input integrity instead of silently dropping numeric values.
- User impact: Calls with a mixed sequence affected by CASA's data loss raise the malformed-record error.
- Owner decision: Standing CASA data-loss rule in AGENTS.md.
- Evidence: [record-sequence-edges-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-sequence-edges-casa), [bugs-record](#quanta-evidence-bugs-record).

##### quanta-record-integer-overflow: Previously agreed

- Record: [CASA masks quantity-record integer overflow with a wrapper error](https://github.com/bglenden/casa-rs/blob/ea0ad2a5158f77c82e5ab3681ef63ab264fb9332/docs/CASA%20%28C%2B%2B%29%20bugs.md#casa-masks-quantity-record-integer-overflow-with-a-wrapper-error)
- Inputs: For example Python integers 2**63, [2**63], or their tuple and nested singleton forms in quantity records.
- CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 can return with a pending OverflowError, leading to a CPython SystemError.
- casa-rs: Raise OverflowError directly for the out-of-range integer. In-range integers keep CASA's signed 32-bit narrowing.
- Rationale: Expose the actual input conversion error to the caller.
- User impact: Callers can handle the range failure as a Python OverflowError.
- Owner decision: Standing rule in AGENTS.md to correct CASA behavior that contradicts its evident intent.
- Evidence: [record-sequence-edges-casa](#quanta-evidence-record-sequence-edges-casa), [bugs-record](#quanta-evidence-bugs-record).

### simulator

#### simulator method implementation

Implementation status is **not behavioral verification**. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing modes or combinations, which raise `NotImplementedError` naming the issue shown; Not implemented raises it for every call; Disabled in CASA and Deprecated in CASA do what CASA does; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Evidence states are listed separately below.

Audit baseline: `30517424209d7531ce6f4c93e1e8ef94a5e4e66b`. Status counts: Implemented: 23, Partial: 6, Not implemented: 0, Disabled in CASA: 3, Deprecated in CASA: 1, Unassessed: 0.

KAntPos accepts offsets but leaves simulated DATA unchanged, as CASA does below its B pivot. EGainCurve acts before leakage; Tsys uses CASA's reversed inversion sense and neutral invalid parameters. Invalid mappings, malformed parameter counts and cubic interior grids on physical axes of four or more channels with fewer than four valid samples raise; shorter physical axes use CASA linear fallback. Corrects the documented natural-spline first-knot defect. Cubic time interiors require four samples; exact/endpoint queries accept shorter axes. Corrects CASA spline-setup and unsynchronized per-scan crashes, retaining atomic failure. Supplied A Noise uses baseline/correlation parameters and the same time/frequency interpolation; supplied M/Mf tables apply inverse parallel-hand gains to the additive side, zero its cross hands, and leave the sky model unchanged below CASA's simulation B pivot. BPOLY uses the data frequency grid; GSPLINE uses legacy amplitude/phase B-splines, reference-frequency scaling and zero outside the fitted interval. Fringe phases advance by rate before time interpolation, then include delay and dispersion. Switched-power application requires the same SYSPOWER/CALDEVICE context as CASA. Factory-only calibration families are outside the demonstrated supplied-table simulation scope. Full polarized matrices use Jp V Jq^H, require all four correlations (circular-feed F is diagonal and also accepts partial products), and substitute identity for an invalid whole matrix; Dgen includes the second-order leakage term.
